## LNK-F-0218

**An `hx-post` control whose handler answers a 4xx does nothing visible at all**

finding · 2026-09-04

cites: [LNK-M-0061](milestones.md#lnk-m-0061)

cites: [LNK-M-0095](milestones.md#lnk-m-0095)

cites: [LNK-D-0415](decisions.md#lnk-d-0415)

cites: [LNK-D-0416](decisions.md#lnk-d-0416)

cites: [LNK-D-0430](decisions.md#lnk-d-0430)

**An `hx-post` control whose handler answers a 4xx does nothing visible at all.** htmx's default `responseHandling` is `[{204,false},{"[23]..",true},{"[45]..",false}]` — a 4xx is read, an error event fires, and no swap happens. Every refusal `webError` writes is a 4xx error *page*, so a reader who clicks **Delete** on a routing rule, a split variant, the link's danger-zone delete, an invitation revoke, a member removal or a dispute reviewer revoke, and is refused with a `403` or a `409`, sees the confirmation dismissed and the page unchanged. The refusal was rendered and thrown away

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0061 *(reopened)* |
| Where | The rule is in the vendored `internal/ui/static/js/htmx.min.js` (search `responseHandling:`) and the config meta at `internal/ui/templates/layout.html:14` does not override it. `internal/httpx/web.go:269-293` (`webError` → `errorPage`, 403/404/409/500); the controls are `partials/link_rules.html:44`, `partials/link_split.html:47,76`, `partials/link_danger.html:29`, `pages/invites.html:89`, `pages/members.html:139`, `partials/dispute_reviewers.html:78` |
| Evidence | Found at LNK-M-0061's reopening while making the QR logo form self-applying. That form is the first in the QR panel to post over htmx, so the rule had to be read; `finishQRAction` now answers 200 for an htmx request so its refusal reaches the page. The same reasoning was not applied outside the panel, because outside the panel is out of this milestone's spec |
| Severity | **Low, and silent — which is what makes it worth a row.** Each of these is a refusal the reader is entitled to and none of them is reachable by an ordinary action: they need a permission the actor lacks or a conflict the page already guards against. The fix has two candidate shapes and picking one is the point of deferring — a shared `webError` limb that answers htmx with a swappable fragment, or an `htmx-config` `responseHandling` entry, which is global and would change how *every* form's 4xx behaves. `hx-target` on each control is a third and worst |
| Reviewed | **Reviewed 2026-09-04**, LNK-M-0095's triage — Tier B, approved for the close (D415, D416). The previous state is what the triage read. |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0095, D430.** `errorPage` answers an htmx request with the flash as a swappable fragment, at `200` — htmx swaps a 2xx and discards everything else, and the refusal already happened, so what the reader is owed is the sentence rather than the status. One limb at the single site every refusal passes through, which is why D430 chose that shape over a global `htmx-config` entry (it would change every form's 4xx, including ones written later against the documented default) and over `hx-target` on each control (six edits, no rule, and the seventh control is written without it). Both halves are pinned: an htmx request gets a fragment, an ordinary navigation still gets its 409. |
| Status | closed |
| LinkCtrl | F218 |

## LNK-F-0223

**A logo pins the code to level H permanently**

cites: [LNK-D-0186](decisions.md#lnk-d-0186)

**A logo pins the code to level H permanently.** Uploading one forces error correction to H, and removing it leaves the code at H forever — a setting the reader never chose and cannot unset from this tab. The owner, asked what the detriment was and given the measurement: *"Always change to the highest reasonable level when the logo leaves, the old QR should still resolve as long as the link stays the same so a change in the new code shouldn't be an issue"*

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | — *(found, post-LNK-M-0062; owner-directed)* |
| Where | `internal/link/qr.go:434`, `:609`, `:699`; the removal path `internal/httpx/web_qr.go:455-458`, `:471-475`, which clears the logo and leaves `Level` where the upload put it |
| Evidence | Found by survey 2026-08-12 and put to the owner with the cost measured against the repo's own encoder: at level M a typical short URL encodes to version 4, 33 modules; at H to version 5, 37 — **~30% more modules a side, ~70% more by area**, so each module is ~30% smaller at a given printed size and the code scans from proportionally less distance. `make verify-scan` already shows dense codes are what fail first |
| Severity | **Low to moderate.** Nothing is broken — an H code scans, it just scans from nearer than it needs to — and the reader has no way to see why. The fix has a rule attached rather than being a one-line revert, which is what makes it a row |
| Reviewed | **Approved as work 2026-08-12**, owner-chosen, into LNK-M-0062's second reopening. The rule is owner-answered: **the highest level that does not grow the symbol**, so correction is taken whenever it is free, and H while a logo is drawn |
| Closed by | **Closed by LNK-M-0062's second reopening, 2026-08-13.** The level is a rule now — the strongest one that does not push the symbol into a larger version — and since D187 it is a **floor under every code** rather than a default for codes that named nothing: the drawn level is the stronger of what the row names and what the rule gives, so `H` is kept where it is needed and nobody, including an API caller, draws less correction than costs nothing. `ClearQRCodeLogo` clears the level with the bytes and re-fits the size against the smaller symbol, in one statement, so a code whose logo leaves goes back to the level its own payload earns rather than staying at the H the upload forced; `TestRemovingALogoRecomputesTheLevelRatherThanKeepingH` reads the row and not only the view. *(**The population this closure does not reach, named at step 3.4 rather than left to be discovered**: a row whose logo was removed by a build older than this one kept its `H`, and a stored `H` binds under the floor, so nothing would recompute it. QR logos have never shipped — `03800_qr_code_logo.sql` landed 2026-08-07, after `v0.2.0`, and 0.3.0 is untagged — so no instance an operator can have holds one, and neither dev instance does: zero rows at `H` with a null logo on demo and on test, checked 2026-08-13. Raised by this milestone's reviewer, which read the closure as unqualified.)* The Where cell's three `internal/link/qr.go` sites are the forcing, which is unchanged and correct. **The half nobody had noticed is that the same `M` was pinned on every code that never had a logo**: `Normalize` wrote the default into every style this product stored, and it stops — but nothing is migrated, because under the floor a stored `M` cannot bind and resolves exactly as an unset one does. `CreateQRCode` no longer copies a logo-forced `H` onto the code it creates, which was this finding rebuilt inside its own fix. Nothing changes size where the floor cannot raise the symbol, which `TestTheRuleNeverChangesTheModuleCount` sweeps the version range for; where it can, every site that fits a size encodes through the rule, and the one row shape that predates that is F232. The tab still does not print the level; it names it where a reader's own action moves it (D186) |
| Status | closed |

## LNK-F-0225

**Creating a second code copies the default's stored size onto a longer payload, so the new code draws at a size nobody set**

finding · 2026-08-13

cites: [LNK-M-0059](milestones.md#lnk-m-0059)

cites: [LNK-M-0063](milestones.md#lnk-m-0063)

cites: [LNK-D-0185](decisions.md#lnk-d-0185)

**Creating a second code copies the default's stored size onto a longer payload, so the new code draws at a size nobody set.** A named code's content carries `&qrc=<slug>` on top of the default's, which can push it into the next symbol version; the copied `size` is then below what the larger symbol needs at the copied `scale`, and `fitGeometry` falls back to the margin-and-scale arithmetic

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0059 *(reopened)* |
| Where | `internal/link/qr.go`, `CreateQRCode` — it reads the default's style through `storedQRStyle` and marshals it whole, `size` included. The fallback is `internal/qr/qr.go`'s `fitGeometry`, which draws `Style.Size` only while the symbol and its quiet zone fit inside it |
| Evidence | Measured 2026-08-13 in `internal/link`: alias `summer` gives a 29-module default code and a 33-module named one. The size control's smallest offer for the default is its own floor, `qr.MinSizeFor(29)` = **70px**, which fits at scale 2. Create a second code and that style draws **82px** — the named symbol's floor at scale 2 is 78. Longer aliases do not reach it, because both payloads land on the same version: `summer-campaign-2026` and a 40-character alias both come out equal |
| Severity | **Low.** It takes a code stored at or near its own floor, which is the bottom of the slider, and the picture is larger rather than unreadable — the quiet zone the fallback draws is `DefaultMargin`, so it still scans. It is a row rather than nothing because it is the same class as the defect this milestone's second reopening exists to fix: a stored size that is not the size drawn. **Out of spec here**: every bullet of the reopening is about the size somebody *requested*, and nobody requests this one — it is inherited. The fix is a decision rather than a patch, and there are three — re-fit the copied style against the new code's own symbol, drop `size` from the copy so the new code takes the default geometry, or refuse the create — which is why it is not taken here |
| Reviewed | **Approved as work 2026-08-13**, in the owner's five answers taken between milestones — *"Re-fit the row whenever the payload changes"*, with the floor allowed to move and the notice owed only where the size must rise. It reopened LNK-M-0059 a third time rather than being taken from LNK-M-0063, the owner choosing the milestone that made the claim over the cheaper route. Of the three fixes this row names, the owner took the first |
| Closed by | **Closed by LNK-M-0059's third reopening, 2026-08-13.** `CreateQRCode` re-fits the style it copies against the created code's *own* payload rather than marshalling the default's whole, so `size` is the size that code draws. `link.refitForPayload` keeps the number wherever the larger symbol admits a scale — 512px on the measured payload keeps 512 and moves the scale 14 → 12 — and raises it to `qr.MinSizeFor` where none does, 70 → 78 on this row's own measurement. Reported then and silent otherwise (D185), through `?qr=added&from=&to=` on the dashboard and `refit` on the create's JSON. Asserted by `TestASizeSurvivesThePayloadGrowingUnderIt` on the arithmetic and `TestAddingACodeReFitsEveryRowItsPayloadChanged` at the call site, the second reading the served SVG's `width` rather than recomputing it |
| Status | closed |
| LinkCtrl | F225 |

**F225's defect moved onto the default code, and the measurement in that row no longer describes it.** F225 is *creating a second code copies the default's stored size onto a longer payload*; after D183 both payloads are the same length, because the default gains an eight-character slug in the same operation — so the copy is exact and the created code is fine. What grows instead is **the default's own payload**, against a `size` fitted before it had a tag. A default code stored at its own floor therefore draws larger than the number the reader set, on the code they set it on

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0060 *(reopened)* |
| Where | Measured 2026-08-13 in `internal/link` against alias `summer`: untagged payload **29 modules**, floor `qr.MinSizeFor(29)` = **70px** at scale 2; tagged payload **33 modules**, floor **78px** at that scale. A style stored at 70/scale 2 draws 70px before the create and **82px** after it, because `fitGeometry` falls back to margin-and-scale once the symbol and its quiet zone no longer fit inside `Style.Size`. `internal/link/qr.go`, `CreateQRCode` — the `NameQRCode` call that gives the default a slug does not re-fit the row it names |
| Evidence | Found by measurement while building LNK-M-0060's reopening, filed rather than fixed. **Out of spec**: every bullet of the reopening is about identity, removability, promotion and what an already-printed picture resolves to, and none of them is about a stored size. It is also not a new class — it is F225's, one code to the left, which is why it is a row pointing at that one rather than a second description of the same thing |
| Severity | **Low, and lower than F225's.** It needs a code stored at or very near its own floor, which is the bottom of the slider, and the picture comes out larger rather than unreadable — the fallback draws `DefaultMargin`, so the quiet zone is the ISO four modules and it still scans. The reason it is a row is that it makes LNK-M-0059's *the requested size is the size stored and drawn, exactly* false in a case LNK-M-0059 could not have known about, and the fix is the same three-way decision F225 names: re-fit the row when it is named, refuse to name it, or say that a stored size is fitted to a payload and a payload can change |
| Reviewed | **Approved as work 2026-08-13** with F225, in the same owner answer and by the same sentence — one rule answers both, which is what that answer gave. Raised at LNK-M-0060's reopening 2026-08-13. Dispositioning it should probably decide F225 at the same time — one rule answers both |
| Closed by | **Closed by LNK-M-0059's third reopening, 2026-08-13.** The half F225's fix does not reach: the default code's own row is re-fitted by `refitStoredQRCode`, written through the upsert's conflict branch so the re-fit cannot rename the code or move the flag. Asked for on **every** create rather than only where `NameQRCode` runs — a row this release inherits is already in this state, and the guard means a row that is already fitted writes nothing. The measurement in this row is the fixture — 29 modules to 33, floor 70 to 78, 82px drawn before — and it is asserted forward rather than described. Same rule, same silence, same notice as F225: D185 |

## LNK-F-0227

**Three narrow gaps around the code that materialises a link's default, all in LNK-M-0060's reopening's own new code**

cites: [LNK-D-0183](decisions.md#lnk-d-0183)

**Three narrow gaps around the code that materialises a link's default, all in LNK-M-0060's reopening's own new code.** (a) `NameQRCode` is `:execrows` and the count is ignored, so a zero-row result is silent — the only constructible path is a racer that already named the row, which is benign, but the same call site checks for a unique violation on the same statement. (b) `CreateQRCode`'s name-then-insert is not transactional: if the `UpsertQRCode` for the *new* code fails, the default keeps a slug it gained with no sibling — the one state D183 says should not exist. *(**Widened 2026-08-13 at LNK-M-0059's third reopening**, which put a third write in the same untransactional run: the sequence is now name-then-**re-fit**-then-insert, so a failed insert can also leave the default carrying a raised size that nothing reported, the caller having returned an error instead. The same window, one more statement inside it — recorded here rather than as a fourth row, because the durable fix is still the one this row already names.)* (c) `materializeDefaultQRCode` has no unique-violation retry, unlike the identical window `SetQRStyleBySlug` guards, so two concurrent *Add another code* calls on a link with no rows give one of them a raw 23505 out of `qr_codes_link_default_key`

| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0060 *(reopened)* |

| Evidence | Found by the second reviewer of LNK-M-0060's reopening, 2026-08-13, reading the three behaviour changes the second attempt made. None of them falsifies a bullet in `m50.md`'s reopening — every one is satisfied by the tree — which is why they are a row rather than a rejection |
| Severity | **Low, and (c) is the only one a reader can reach.** (c) is a 500 on a race two people would have to run into within one service call on a link with no `qr_codes` rows at all; (a) and (b) are silent and benign on every path either reviewer could construct. The reason they are one row is that all three are the same shape — the file reasons about this exact race twice and guards it once — so the durable fix is a rule about where that guard belongs, not three patches |

**Renaming a link is the other payload change, and no code's stored size is re-fitted for it**

finding · 2026-08-13

cites: [LNK-M-0059](milestones.md#lnk-m-0059)

cites: [LNK-F-0225](#lnk-f-0225)

cites: [LNK-F-0226](#lnk-f-0226)

cites: [LNK-M-0095](milestones.md#lnk-m-0095)

**Renaming a link is the other payload change, and no code's stored size is re-fitted for it.** LNK-M-0059's third reopening re-fits where a *slug* is written, which is `CreateQRCode`. An alias change grows every one of that link's codes' payloads by exactly the same mechanism — a longer short URL is more bytes in the picture — so a code stored at or near its own floor draws larger than the number the reader set, on a link they renamed for unrelated reasons

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0059 *(reopened)* |
| Where | `internal/link/service.go`, `Update` — `newAlias` is written and the cache invalidated (`:830-833`), and nothing reads `qr_codes`. The drawing then falls back through `internal/qr/qr.go`'s `fitGeometry`, which is the same fallback F225 and F226 named |
| Evidence | Measured 2026-08-13 in `internal/link` with the arithmetic F226 used: `https://links.example/summer` is 29 modules untagged and its floor is 70px; extending the alias by twelve characters reaches 33 modules, whose floor is 78px, so a row stored at 70 draws 82. `qr.Style.Size`'s own doc names this case in as many words — *a link whose alias grew encodes to a larger matrix* — and `SetQRSizeBySlug`'s comment has described the fallback as the intended behaviour since LNK-M-0059 shipped, which is why this is a row rather than an oversight inside the diff |
| Severity | **Low, and out of spec for the third reopening** — the boundary is textual: the bullet is *every path that lengthens a payload re-fits **the row it touches***, and an alias change touches the `links` row and no `qr_codes` row; the reopening's own risk section names its reach as *wherever a slug is written, promoted or cleared*. Taking it would have put a QR re-fit, and a size-rise notice, inside the link edit form and the link PUT — two surfaces no bullet mentions. Same shape and same severity as F225: it needs a code at the bottom of the slider, and the picture comes out larger rather than unreadable, because the fallback draws `DefaultMargin`. It is a row because it makes the same shipped claim false — *the requested size is the size stored and drawn, exactly* — through a door the fix did not close, and because the fix for it is one call to the `refitForPayload` that now exists |
| Reviewed | **Reviewed 2026-09-04**, LNK-M-0095's triage — Tier B, approved for the close (D415, D416). The previous state is what the triage read. |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0095.** `Service.RefitQRCodesForPayload` re-fits every code a link carries, called from `Update` after the transaction when the alias changed — best-effort, because a re-fit that failed must not undo a rename, and the codes self-repair on the next touch. Driven end to end by `TestARenameRefitsThisLinksQRCodes`. **The test took three attempts and the first two are worth recording**: `qrCodeFrom` reports the size the picture is *drawn* at, so comparing it against a floor compares a value with itself, and both early versions passed against the unfixed tree. The invariant is the **stored** size against the drawn one, and the code has to be pinned to its own floor first or it has headroom and the defect is unreachable. Without the fix: *the row stores 280px and the picture draws 328px*. |

## LNK-F-0232

**A code whose style names level `L` now draws larger than the size stored on it**

finding · 2026-08-13

cites: [LNK-D-0187](decisions.md#lnk-d-0187)

cites: [LNK-M-0062](milestones.md#lnk-m-0062)

cites: [LNK-M-0059](milestones.md#lnk-m-0059)

cites: [LNK-D-0129](decisions.md#lnk-d-0129)

cites: [LNK-F-0225](#lnk-f-0225)

cites: [LNK-F-0226](#lnk-f-0226)

cites: [LNK-F-0228](#lnk-f-0228)

cites: [LNK-D-0186](decisions.md#lnk-d-0186)

**A code whose style names level `L` now draws larger than the size stored on it.** D187 makes the level a floor, so an `L` row is drawn at the strongest free level — never below `M`. Its stored `size` was fitted against `L`'s own, smaller symbol by a release where `L` meant `L`, and once the symbol widens the size no longer contains it and its quiet zone, so `fitGeometry` falls back to margin-and-scale and the picture measures something else

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0062 *(reopened)* |
| Where | `internal/qr/qr.go`, `encode` (the floor) against `fitGeometry`'s `st.Size >= symbol+2*MinMarginModules*st.Scale` guard. Every *write* path is safe and was checked one by one: `SetQRSizeBySlug`, `storeQRStyle`, `refitForPayload`, `refitForLogo` and `refitFromLogo` all fit against `qr.Encode(content, level)`, which applies the floor — so only a row written before this release is exposed |
| Evidence | Measured 2026-08-13 through the shipping path on `https://lnk.io/ab3x9?src=qr`: `L` alone is 25 modules and the free level is 29. `qr.FitSize(25, 300)` gives scale 9, and a style holding `{level:L, size:300, scale:9}` now needs `qr.MinSizeForStyle(29, scale 9)` = **315px**; `qr.Drawn` reports **333px** for a row that says 300. Reachable only for a row an API caller wrote naming `L` — nothing else has ever put that string in a style. *(**Bounded at step 3.4 by this milestone's reviewer and the orchestrator**, which is what makes it low rather than moderate: the defect needs `level:L` **and** a stored `size`, and `size` is LNK-M-0059's, unreleased. `v0.2.0` is the newest tag, so no upgrade path can hold the pair. Both instances checked 2026-08-13 — `select count(*) filter (where style->>'level'='L')` over `qr_codes` returns **0** on demo and on test. The reviewer's independent sweep found **1828 of 2541** (payload, size) pairs would draw ~11% larger across the whole size range, not only near the floor — that is the breadth **if** such a row existed, and none does.)* |
| Severity | **Low, and out of spec.** It needs a caller who used `PUT …/qr` to ask for `L`, which the dashboard has never offered (D129), and the picture comes out *larger* rather than unreadable — the fallback draws `DefaultMargin`, so the quiet zone is the ISO four modules and it still scans. It is a row because it makes LNK-M-0059's *the requested size is the size stored and drawn, exactly* false for a row shape this milestone could not write and did not repair, which is F225/F226/F228's class through a fourth door. **No migration can fix it**: the repair is a re-fit and a re-fit needs the encoder, so the candidate shapes are a re-fit on next touch (`refitStoredQRCode` already exists and is already called unconditionally from `CreateQRCode`) or a one-off backfill command |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** Raised at LNK-M-0062's second reopening, 2026-08-13, in D186's account of what the floor costs LNK-M-0059 |
| Status | open |
| LinkCtrl | F232 |

finding · 2026-08-13

cites: [LNK-D-0415](decisions.md#lnk-d-0415)

cites: [LNK-D-0416](decisions.md#lnk-d-0416)

**`make verify-scan`'s control half no longer covers four levels, and two decisions say it does.** The control draws every version at each of `L`, `M`, `Q` and `H`; since D187 the `L` slot resolves to the free level and is byte for byte the `M` slot's picture, so the half covers three distinct levels with one duplicate a version. D181 and D182 both describe it as *over the whole version range at every level*

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0062 *(reopened)* |
| Where | `internal/qr/scancorpus_test.go`, the control loop's `for _, level := range Levels`; the sentences are `Plan.md`'s D181 (*"It reads the control clean at both — 1496 of 1496, over the whole version range at every level"*) and D182 (*"reads the no-logo control 2316 of 2316"*) |

The manifest records the level *drawn*, so nothing in the output claims otherwise — the loose word is in the two decisions, which are append-only records of measurements taken before the floor existed |
| Severity | **Very low, and documentary.** No coverage is lost: `L` is a level this product can no longer draw at all, so a control at `L` would be testing a picture nobody gets. What it costs is 170 redundant renders and their decodes in a gate that already takes minutes. The row exists because the durable fix is a choice — drop the slot and restate the corpus counts three documents quote, or keep it and say in the corpus what *every level* now means — and because a claim that has gone loose is exactly what nobody notices |
| Reviewed | **Reviewed 2026-09-04**, LNK-M-0095's triage — Tier B, approved for the close (D415, D416). The previous state is what the triage read. |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0095.** Answered by the second of the two shapes this row offers: the corpus keeps its 1360 pictures and states what *every level* means where the next reader meets it, and the two loose sentences are corrected by a new decisions entry, since D181 and D182 are append-only records of measurements that were correctly taken. **This row's cite is corrected too** — it placed the two sentences in `Plan.md` and they are in `decisions.md`. |

LNK-M-0062's own contract is that a logo'd code's **row** holds H, which is why `TestALogoRaisesTheCodeToLevelHAndSaysSo` reads `qr_codes` directly rather than the service

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0062 *(reopened)* |

| Evidence | **It predates this diff**: before 0.3.0 the same statement wrote `"level":"M"` onto a logo'd row, which is the same distance from `H` and the same disagreement. What changed is only the string. Read 2026-08-13 against both versions of `Normalize` |
| Severity | **Low, and out of spec.** The picture is right — `internal/qr` forces `H` at the renderer precisely so a row that says otherwise cannot draw an under-corrected code — so what is wrong is the row and the `GET` that reads it *(the `GET` is right too: `qrCodeFrom` applies `ForLogo` on read)*. It is a row rather than a two-line fix because the same reset also has to decide what happens to a stored `size` fitted against `H`'s symbol, which is F232's arithmetic on a path that is not F232's |
| Reviewed | **Reviewed 2026-09-04**, LNK-M-0095's triage — Tier B, approved for the close (D415, D416). The previous state is what the triage read. |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0095.** `ResetQRStyleBySlug` applies `ForLogo` when the row carries one, and re-fits the size with it — a size fitted against H's larger symbol is not a size the defaults hold, which is the second half this row names. Asserted against the `qr_codes` column rather than the service, because `qrCodeFrom` applies `ForLogo` on read and would report H either way. Sabotage-verified: without the branch the row holds `""`. |

## LNK-F-0236

**Text in a code's row can no longer be selected with the mouse, including the printed slug**

finding · 2026-08-14

cites: [LNK-M-0063](milestones.md#lnk-m-0063)

**Text in a code's row can no longer be selected with the mouse, including the printed slug.** Making the row one click target (F224f) stretches the name's anchor over the whole row with an `::after` overlay, which is the one way to widen a link's target without nesting interactive elements — and an overlay over the row is also an overlay over its text, so dragging across the meta line starts a drag on the link instead of a selection. The slug is the string a reader is most likely to want to copy: it is what the code prints and what `?qrc=` carries

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0063 |
| Where | `internal/ui/templates/partials/link_qr.html`, the row anchor's `after:absolute after:inset-0` against the meta line below it, which renders `<code>{{.Slug}}</code>` |
| Evidence | The overlay is what `TestARowSelectsOnItsWholeArea` asserts and what the owner asked for, so this is the cost of the fix rather than a mistake in it. Not measured in a browser — it follows from the overlay, and the row's own spec drives the click it exists for rather than the selection it prevents |
| Severity | **Low, and out of spec.** The slug is reachable three other ways: selecting the code opens the panel with `?code=<slug>` in the address bar, the download filenames carry it, and the API answers it. The fix is a choice rather than a repair — lifting the meta line above the overlay with `relative` restores selection and puts a strip of the row back outside the click target, which is the affordance the owner reported. Both halves cannot be had from one overlay, so somebody has to say which matters more |

Read from the source; not driven, because there is nothing in the tree today that the regexp misses |
| Severity | **Low, and latent.** No popover in the tree escapes it now, so nothing is currently unasserted; what the row records is that the guard is narrower than the sentence beside it. This replaces the current 'Add another code' label/text field/Add code button."* (i) *"The tooltip on the default button should just say 'Default QR Code' and 'Make Default QR Code' when not a default. The button also needs a more lenient tooltip zone as it is difficult to get the tooltip to show. Anywhere a click on the button would be accepted should also show the tooltip when hovered for a short period."* (j) *"The highlighting for the download and remove buttons is only visible when not on the selected row."*

**A typed size outside the range is refused only while the slider has not been dragged.** Three records this milestone writes say the out-of-range refusal is what the one-way mirror buys, and it is — but only from a form nobody has touched. **Reproduction:** open a link's QR tab, drag the **Size** slider to any value X, then type `9999` into the number box beside it, then press **Save**. The slider is already off `size_shown`, so the slider wins whatever the box says: **X is stored, and no refusal is produced.** The reader who typed 9999 is told nothing, and the size they get is one they set earlier by a different gesture

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Dated | on import: the row carries no date |
| Found in | LNK-M-0064 |
| Where | `internal/httpx/web_qr.go:350-361` (`requestedQRSize`; `:357` is `if shown := formInt(...); slider != shown { return slider }`). | Evidence | **The behaviour is LNK-M-0059's and predates LNK-M-0064 entirely** — `git log -S 'size_shown' internal/httpx/web_qr.go` puts the witness rule at LNK-M-0059's reopening, and nothing in this diff touches `requestedQRSize`'s body. What LNK-M-0064 changed is visibility: until the script existed neither input ever moved on its own, so the divergence between the box and the slider was never on screen. `tools/agent-browser/specs/qr-tab-controls.spec.mjs` drives exactly this sequence — drag, then type out of range — and deliberately stops before the save, because saving is where the disagreement is and asserting it would be asserting the defect |
| Severity | **Low, and a design question rather than a bug to patch.** Nothing is lost or corrupted: a size the reader themselves set is stored. What is wrong is that a number they typed is discarded in silence, where the same number typed a second earlier would have been refused with a sentence. The fix is not local — it is a third state for the arbitration (*the box was edited last*), which means the form has to carry which input moved most recently, which is a second witness and a decision about whether the server may trust a script's account of an ordering |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** Out of LNK-M-0064's spec: the milestone's bullet is that the two inputs follow each other, and they do. Filed at that milestone's second rejection, which is where the condition was first stated correctly in the three records that had claimed it unconditionally |

## LNK-F-0241

**The tab's own tooltips announce their control's name a second time, and their hosts are unnamed generic elements to a keyboard**

finding · 2026-09-13

cites: [LNK-M-0064](milestones.md#lnk-m-0064)

cites: [LNK-D-0192](decisions.md#lnk-d-0192)

**The tab's own tooltips announce their control's name a second time, and their hosts are unnamed generic elements to a keyboard.** Two symptoms of one pattern. (a) Every tooltip host pairs an `aria-label` with an `aria-describedby` tooltip carrying the **same string** — `aria-label="Default QR Code"` beside a tooltip reading `Default QR Code`, `aria-label="Add a QR code"` beside `Add a QR code` — so a screen reader announces name-then-description, identical. (b) Every `.qr-tip-host` wrapping a **disabled** control is a `tabindex="0"` `<span>` with no `role` and no accessible name of its own, so a keyboard tabbing through the list lands on a generic, unnamed element and hears the tooltip with nothing to attach it to

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Dated | on import: the row carries no date |
| Found in | LNK-M-0064 |
| Where | `internal/ui/templates/partials/link_qr.html:171-177` and `:200-206` (the `+`, both states), `:351-357` (the default icon), `:401-408` (remove on a link's last code), `:437-453` (the `links.read` pair). The `tabindex="0"` hosts are the disabled ones — a disabled button cannot take focus, which is why the wrapper takes it |
| Evidence | Read against the rendered template rather than inferred: the two live tooltips whose text differs from their control's name are the *reasons* — `Every link must have at least 1 QR code.` and `A link carries at most 20 QR codes.` — and those are the ones the pattern was built for (D192). The duplicated pair is the other four, where the tooltip exists to be a hover target of button size rather than to say anything new |
| Severity | **Low, and it follows from D192 rather than contradicting it.** D192 chose a tooltip this page owns precisely so a *disabled* control could explain itself, and a focusable wrapper is the only way a disabled button's description is ever reached. Both symptoms are the cost of that, not a departure from it — which is why this is a row and not a fix inside the milestone that wrote the pattern. Fixing (a) means either dropping `aria-describedby` where the strings match, or giving those four tooltips something to say that the name does not; fixing (b) means a `role` and a name on the host, or a different focus target entirely |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** Neither symptom falsifies a bullet in m50.8.md — the tooltip renders, shows on hover anywhere over the button and shows on focus where the button refuses it, which is what the milestone claims. It is the announcement *quality* underneath that claim, and it needs the owner to say whether a redundant description is worse than a missing one |
| Status | open |
| LinkCtrl | F241 |

## LNK-F-0242

**`make verify-ui` has two sign-ins of headroom left against `LOGIN_RATE_PER_MIN`, and nothing in the suite knows it**

finding · 2026-09-13

cites: [LNK-M-0064](milestones.md#lnk-m-0064)

cites: [LNK-D-0193](decisions.md#lnk-d-0193)

**`make verify-ui` has two sign-ins of headroom left against `LOGIN_RATE_PER_MIN`, and nothing in the suite knows it.** The whole kept suite runs in well under a minute from one address and performs **8** sign-ins against a default limit of **10**. The ninth and tenth are free; the eleventh fails, and it fails *every* spec at its sign-in step with a message saying the credentials are wrong — which is the one thing that will not be true. There is no assertion, no comment in the runner and no target-level guard that would name the real cause

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Dated | on import: the row carries no date |
| Found in | LNK-M-0064 |
| Where | Counted against the tree: one sign-in each in `tools/agent-browser/specs/link-tabs.spec.mjs`, `workspace-control.spec.mjs` and `qr-logo.spec.mjs`, three in `qr-codes-list.spec.mjs` (one per case), two in `qr-tab-controls.spec.mjs` (a shared serial page, plus the script-blocked case's own context). The limit is `LOGIN_RATE_PER_MIN`, default 10 |
| Evidence | Found the hard way while LNK-M-0064's spec was written: a sign-in per case pushed the run over and every file went red at sign-in at once. The immediate answer was to share one signed-in page across that file's scripted cases, which is a per-file fix for a suite-wide budget — the next spec to be added will be written the way the other four were, and nothing it can read says why that is now too expensive |
| Severity | **Low today, and it goes off without warning.** No product behaviour is wrong; the limiter is doing what it is for. What is missing is that a shared, exhaustible budget is spent by files that do not know about each other, and the failure mode blames the account. Options are all cheap and none is obviously right: raise the limit for the test instance in `.env.test` and pin the reason to it; share one signed-in storage state across the whole suite through a Playwright global setup; or assert the count in the runner so adding a ninth sign-in fails on the count rather than on a lie |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** Out of LNK-M-0064's spec, which owns one spec file and not the suite's budget. Filed at that milestone's second rejection, where the current number was counted; D193 and `tools/agent-browser/README.md` both now state it, which is the interim measure — the number is written down where the next author meets it, but nothing enforces it |
| Status | open |
| LinkCtrl | F242 |

## LNK-F-0243

**The list sorts by the name a reader gave, and draws one they did not**

finding · 2026-09-13

cites: [LNK-M-0064](milestones.md#lnk-m-0064)

**The list sorts by the name a reader gave, and draws one they did not.** `ORDER BY lower(q.label), q.id` sorts on the **stored** label, but a row whose label is empty renders a substitute — `The original code` for the default, `Unnamed code` for any other. Nothing requires a name at the add form, so a second unnamed code is reachable in two clicks. A link holding two unnamed codes and one called *Autumn poster* then lists, top to bottom: **Unnamed code**, **The original code**, **Autumn poster** — placeholders first in id order, which is alphabetical by nothing on screen, and the two placeholders are not even in alphabetical order with each other

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Dated | on import: the row carries no date |
| Found in | LNK-M-0064 |
| Where | `internal/store/query/campaigns.sql:174` is the sort; `internal/httpx/web_links.go:1281-1288` (`qrCodeViews`) is the substitution; `internal/ui/templates/partials/link_qr.html:190-193` is the add form's label input, which carries `maxlength` and no `required` |
| Evidence | Read against the tree at LNK-M-0064's third attempt, not reproduced in a browser. `api/openapi.yaml:5937-5938` **states the carve-out** — *"A code nobody has named sorts first"* — so the API surface is accurate and always was. `docs/usage.md:342` did not, and was corrected in LNK-M-0064's own diff at step 3.4 to say the same thing. The integration test at `test/integration/qr_test.go:2199-2215` covers exactly one unnamed code, the default, whose placement is identical under either reading — so the two-unnamed-codes case is unasserted rather than asserted wrongly |
| Severity | **Low, and it is a design question the milestone's bullet does not reach.** LNK-M-0064's bullet names `lower(q.label)` as the sort and the tree does that, so nothing is unbuilt. What is open is whether sorting on a value the reader cannot see is what *"alphabetical order by name"* should mean when the product itself puts a different word on the row. Three answers and none is free: sort on the substituted name, which moves the substitution into SQL or the sort into Go; require a label at the add form, which is a behaviour change and reaches the API; or keep it and accept that unnamed codes cluster first, which is what the API has always promised |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** Filed by the orchestrator at LNK-M-0064's third review, from that reviewer's finding. Out of spec by the bullet, in scope for whoever decides what a name is |
| Status | open |
| LinkCtrl | F243 |

## LNK-F-0245

**Four fields on the QR view are filled on every render and read by no template — and their doc comments described a panel that stated them**

finding · 2026-09-13

cites: [LNK-F-0244](#lnk-f-0244)

cites: [LNK-M-0064](milestones.md#lnk-m-0064)

cites: [LNK-F-0239](#lnk-f-0239)

**Four fields on the QR view are filled on every render and read by no template — and their doc comments described a panel that stated them.** `QRSourceLabel` fed the analytics sentence and `QRMaxLogoBytes`, `QRMaxLogoDimension` and `QRMaxLogoPixels` fed the logo's limits paragraph; F244(c) and F244(f) removed both paragraphs, so `linkQR` still computes and passes all four and nothing renders any of them. **The comments are corrected in this diff and the fields are not**, which is the split the row rests on: prose this diff made false is this diff's to fix, and deleting a struct field is not a prose removal. So what a reader opening this row finds is four live fields whose comments already say nothing reads them, pointing here. Nothing is broken — the values are cheap constants — but a view struct that carries fields no surface reads is how the next reader learns the wrong thing about what the page shows

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Dated | on import: the row carries no date |
| Found in | LNK-M-0064 *(reopened)* |
| Where | `internal/httpx/web_links.go:637` and `:727-729` declare them, `:1136` and `:1142-1144` assign them; `internal/ui/templates/partials/link_qr.html` read them at `:43` and `:850` before this reopening. The comments are `:630-636` and `:712-726` — as they stood they asserted, present tense, that these were *"passed in … so the numbers the panel states and the ones internal/qr enforces cannot drift"* and that *"the panel's prose has to say which is which"*, of a panel that states none of them after F244(f) |
| Evidence | `grep -rn 'QRSourceLabel\|QRMaxLogoBytes\|QRMaxLogoDimension\|QRMaxLogoPixels' internal/ui/templates/` returns nothing after the diff, against four hits before it. The fixtures in `internal/ui/ui_test.go:715` and `:794` still supply `QRSourceLabel`, which is what a fixture for a field nothing renders looks like. Found while removing the two paragraphs, and out of spec by the milestone's own *no change to what a logo does* and *the tab says less* bounds — deleting struct fields is not a prose removal |
| Severity | **Low, and it is tidiness with one real edge.** No behaviour depends on any of the four and `qr.MaxLogoUploadBytes` is still enforced where it matters. ## LNK-F-0247

**The first write after a page load returns the reader to their offset and shows them different content there, because the notice that write renders grows the page above the card**

finding · 2026-08-17

cites: [LNK-D-0196](decisions.md#lnk-d-0196)

cites: [LNK-M-0064](milestones.md#lnk-m-0064)

**The first write after a page load returns the reader to their offset and shows them different content there, because the notice that write renders grows the page above the card.** D196 restores the document offset faithfully; it is the document that changed. A `?qr=` marker renders a flash at the **top of the page**, above the tab strip, so on the first write after a load everything below it moves down by that notice's height and the restored offset is pointing a screen's worth lower than the reader was reading. The second write does not shift, because the notice was already there before and after

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | — *(owner-reported, post-LNK-M-0064's second reopening)* |
| Where | `internal/ui/templates/pages/link_detail.html:32` is `{{template "flash_ok" .Notice}}`, rendered before `link_tabs.html`'s `#link-tabs` and therefore before `#qr`; `internal/httpx/web_qr.go:581`'s `qrNotice` is what fills it from the marker `qrReturn` puts on every write's redirect; the position stored and applied is `window.scrollY`, a document offset, at `internal/ui/static/js/qr-size.js:97-100` and `:229` |
| Evidence | Owner-reported 2026-08-17 against the running product, unprompted, while confirming the flash on save is gone: *"Changing the default QR code doesn't scroll the page anymore (unless a notification is added for the first change after the screen is loaded)."* The mechanism is read off the tree above and the *first write only* asymmetry is what confirms it — a shift that happened on every write would not be the notice, and one that never happened would not be a notice above the card |
| Severity | **Low, and it is the residue of a claim that is otherwise kept.** Nothing jumps and nothing is lost; the reader is returned to a position that has stopped meaning what it meant, by the height of one sentence, once per load. The fix is to remember the offset **relative to the card** rather than to the document — `#qr`'s top plus a delta, re-measured on the way in — which survives any content arriving above it and not just this notice. Doing it inside `qr-size.js` costs nothing on the wire and replaces two arithmetic lines; the reason it is a row and not an edit is that it changes what a stored offset *means*, and D196's browser case asserts against the document offset it currently is |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed, and deferred by the owner at the moment it was reported.** 2026-08-17, offered as a third limb of LNK-M-0064's third reopening and declined: *"I will address the notifications later as they are only visible if you notice them at the top of the page which can be a problem."* Named as *deliberately not done* in m50.8.md's third reopening so the exclusion is visible from the work as well as from here |
| Status | open |
| LinkCtrl | F247 |

cites: [LNK-M-0078](milestones.md#lnk-m-0078)

cites: [LNK-D-0202](decisions.md#lnk-d-0202)

**`make check-links` proves an anchor exists, not that the row a sentence points at is in the table it names.** `deferred-findings.md` has two tables under two anchors, `#open` and `#closed`, and a row moves between them as its whole lifecycle. Every link to `#open` resolves forever, whichever table the finding is actually in, so a sentence saying *"the row stays open"* beside a link that lands on the Closed table is green

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0064 *(reopened)* |
| Where | `scripts/check-links.sh` resolves the fragment against the target file's headings; nothing reads the tables' rows. The three sites this milestone's third reopening got wrong: `Plan.md:1111`, `docs/build-notes/phase-details/README.md:33` and `:89`, each of them an F246 link spelled `#open` after the same diff closed F246 |
| Evidence | Found by the milestone's reviewer on 2026-08-17, after `make check-links` passed on the tree carrying all three. Reproduced by reading the script: it has no notion of what an `#open` anchor's table contains. The same shape reaches every tracker with more than one section — `workflow-changes.md`'s Proposed/Made, and this file. **Counted at LNK-M-0074's reopened run, 2026-08-17, rather than left as three: the tree carries 39 of them.** Every link in tracked Markdown whose target is this file's `#open` or `#closed` anchor was resolved against the section its row is actually in — 22 are in `decisions.md`, which is append-only and was correct when each was written, and **17 are in files that are maintained**: `Plan.md` ×3 (F178, F222, F223) and nine milestone files (m37, m46.6 ×2, m47.5, m48, m49 ×2, m50, m50.5, m50.6, m50.7, m50.8 ×3). All 17 point at **Open** for a row that is **Closed**; none points the other way. The detector is thirty lines and is what a gate would be |
| Severity | **Low, and it degrades the one check this project uses to keep its records honest.** No product behaviour, and the failure is silent by construction: the reader follows the link, lands on a table, and does not find the row unless they look. What makes it worth a row rather than a habit is that it is *checkable* — the anchor and the row are both in tracked markdown, and a check that looked for the finding's own row inside the table under the heading each link names would have caught every site. Fix note: the linter would need to know which anchors are row tables, which is a per-file list and is the reason this is a row rather than an edit |
| Reviewed | **Reviewed and scheduled 2026-08-17**, at LNK-M-0074's triage, after this run counted the class from three to 39. **Both halves, which is more than was recommended for the cheap option and is the owner's answer**: the row-membership check goes into `check-links` so the class cannot recur, and the **17 links in maintained files** are corrected — `Plan.md` and the nine milestone files. The 22 in `decisions.md` are left, that file being append-only and each having been true when written. The stated cost is a new failure mode on a gate that already resolves 3568 links, taken deliberately, because `check-links` passing is exactly what hid this twice |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0078**, 2026-08-18. `scripts/check-links.sh` gained a third pass: for a link whose fragment is a row-table anchor it reads the rows under that anchor and fails when the row the link text names is in the other table. The per-file list of which anchors are row tables is in the script, which is what this row's fix note said it would need. **The 39 was 83**, counted rather than trusted the way the fix asked: this row's scan did not count the links *inside this file*, and 63 of them were here — every one an `#open` citation to a row since closed. All of them were corrected, D202's principle applied to the population as counted rather than to the number it was counted at; `decisions.md` is exempt as a source, being append-only, and its 22 stand. The check was shown red before the corrections and red again on a deliberate wrong-section link, restored by counter-edit |
| Status | closed |
| LinkCtrl | F248 |

## LNK-F-0250

**Every code selection now stores a scroll offset, and a selection whose swap never arrives leaves it behind for an unrelated later load**

finding · 2026-08-17

cites: [LNK-D-0196](decisions.md#lnk-d-0196)

cites: [LNK-M-0064](milestones.md#lnk-m-0064)

cites: [LNK-M-0074](milestones.md#lnk-m-0074)

cites: [LNK-F-0249](#lnk-f-0249)

cites: [LNK-D-0205](decisions.md#lnk-d-0205)

**Every code selection now stores a scroll offset, and a selection whose swap never arrives leaves it behind for an unrelated later load.** `remember()` fires on `htmx:beforeRequest` from anything inside `#qr`, which the codes list is; `forget()` fires on `htmx:afterSwap`, which a 5xx, an aborted request or a reader who navigates away never produces. The offset is keyed to the link page's own pathname, so the **next** load of that page takes D196's paint hold and settles where the reader stood during a selection they have forgotten making

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0064 *(reopened)* |
| Where | `internal/ui/static/js/qr-size.js:129` (`htmx:beforeRequest` to `remember`), `:157` (`htmx:afterSwap` to `forget`), `:105` (the pathname key), `:268-274` (the hold applied on the strength of a stored offset). The row anchor is inside `#qr` and issues htmx requests since `internal/ui/templates/partials/link_qr.html:273-276` |
| Evidence | Found by the milestone's reviewer on 2026-08-17. **Not new in kind** — the refused logo upload has the same shape and `:148-157` was written for exactly it — but selection changes the frequency from a rare failed write to every click on a row, and the codes list is this tab's most-used control |
| Severity | **Low, and bounded by the three reveals D196 argues.** The stale hold cannot outlast the four-second timer, so the worst case is a page held on its own background a moment longer than it should be and then landing at an offset the reader did not choose. The fix is to forget on the request's end rather than on its success — `htmx:afterRequest` fires on every response including a refusal — but that is the event D196 deliberately did **not** use, on the argument that the swap is the observable fact and does not depend on which htmx event runs first. Reversing a written argument is not a one-word edit |
| Reviewed | **Reviewed and scheduled 2026-08-17**, at LNK-M-0074's triage, into **LNK-M-0064's fourth reopening** with F249. The fix reverses a written argument rather than editing a line, so D196's reasoning about which htmx event is the observable fact is superseded in writing or it is not superseded at all |
| Closed by | **Closed by LNK-M-0064's fourth reopening, 2026-08-17.** `qr-size.js` forgets the offset on `htmx:afterRequest` rather than on `htmx:afterSwap`, and D205 supersedes D196's *the swap is the observable fact* in writing rather than editing it: a swap is observable only when there is one, and the endings this file has to forget for produce none. Guarded on `HX-Redirect` and `HX-Refresh`, because htmx fires the ending **before** the navigation those headers ask for — unguarded, the fix would have dropped the offset on every accepted logo upload, which nothing asserted until this reopening added it to `qr-logo.spec.mjs`. The new browser case drives the refusal itself rather than waiting for a real 5xx, and asserts the offset was **present** in flight so it cannot pass on a mechanism that never ran. **One of the four endings this row names is closed without being claimed** — a reader who navigates away mid-request is the one whose handler would have to run while the document is torn down, and nothing demonstrates that it does; D205 names it as the finding's and leaves it out of the fix's coverage |
| Status | closed |
| LinkCtrl | F250 |

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |

The two that drifted silently are *the size slider draws a visible mark at each stop* (`:257`, second reopening, `5c73c63`) and *selecting a code redraws the tab without leaving the page* (`:991`, third reopening, `3b2174f`); the README last changed at `928504f`, the first reopening |

The fix is small and mechanical: count `^test(` and `^ test(` per spec file, read the bolded count out of the README row, and fail when they differ — a shell gate in the shape of `scripts/check-links.sh`, hung off `make check`. ## LNK-F-0253

**Run the way `docs/releasing.md` offers it, `release-check` silently skips the integration tests**

finding · 2026-08-17

cites: [LNK-M-0075](milestones.md#lnk-m-0075)

**Run the way `docs/releasing.md` offers it, `release-check` silently skips the integration tests.** The script decides whether to run them by asking `docker compose` whether a service called `postgres` is up, and that question only resolves when `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` and `COMPOSE_ENV_FILES` are in the environment. The Makefile exports both; a shell does not. So the last gate before a tag reports `skip  Postgres is not running` on a machine where it is, and the skip reads as information rather than as a gate that did not run

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0075 *(reopened)* |
| Where | `scripts/release-check.sh:229-234` asks `docker compose ps --status running --services`; `Makefile:36-38` is where `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` and `COMPOSE_ENV_FILES` are exported; `docs/releasing.md:44` offers `scripts/release-check.sh v0.3.0` as the equal alternative to `make release-check VERSION=v0.3.0` |
| Evidence | **Run, not argued.** Both forms were run on 2026-08-17 against a stack that was up. `bash scripts/release-check.sh v0.3.0` printed `skip Postgres is not running (docker compose up -d)`; the same `docker compose ps --status running --services` with the Makefile's two variables set printed `postgres`. `docker ps` lists `linkctrl-test-postgres-1` running throughout. The same shape hit this script once before and is written into the Makefile's own comment at `Makefile:686-693`: it ran `go test` with no `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, and the answer taken then was to export it from the Makefile rather than have the script build its own — which is exactly what leaves the direct form short |
| Severity | **Medium, and it is the gate rather than the product.** Nothing is wrong with the integration suite; what is wrong is that the pre-tag gate can report a clean run without having run a third of itself, on the path the documentation names. It fails silent, which is the direction that matters — a release cut this way is untested against a database and nothing says so. The fix is a choice between the script deriving the project itself and the documentation dropping the direct form, and that is a decision rather than an edit |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed when filed.** Filed 2026-08-17 during LNK-M-0075's reopening, whose gate proof required running the script directly and is how the skip was seen at all. **Approved as work 2026-08-18** at Phase 4's planning, grouped with F248, F254 and F255 into one early milestone; the repair shape is the owner's, asked and answered the same day. |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0078**, 2026-08-18, D212. The script derives `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`, `COMPOSE_ENV_FILES` and — the layer below, which the skip was hiding — `TEST_DATABASE_URL` and `LINKCTRL_REDIS_URL`, an already-exported value still winning. A new step, *the Makefile and this script agree about which stack*, fails when either derivation drifts from the Makefile's, which is the accepted cost made into a gate; sabotage-verified by changing `PROJECT` and `COMPOSE_ENV_FILES` in the Makefile and watching it go red. Both documented forms were **run** against an up stack on 2026-08-18 and both ran the integration tests. The skip also gained a third outcome, because *no DSN could be built* and *Postgres is down* are different failures |

## LNK-F-0256

**The single-instance conformance check breaks its readiness wait on Postgres's *temporary* server, then confirms against the gap that follows it**

finding · 2026-08-18

cites: [LNK-M-0075](milestones.md#lnk-m-0075)

cites: [LNK-M-0072](milestones.md#lnk-m-0072)

**The single-instance conformance check breaks its readiness wait on Postgres's *temporary* server, then confirms against the gap that follows it.** `scripts/single-instance-check.sh:93-96` loops until `pg_isready` succeeds and **breaks**; `:97` then re-runs it once as a confirmation and fails the whole check if it says no. Those are two different servers. `postgres:17-alpine` runs `initdb` against a temporary server on first boot, which answers `pg_isready`, then shuts it down and starts the real one — so the loop can break on the temporary server and the confirming line can land in the window where nothing is listening. Whether it does is decided by where the one-second cadence falls, which is why it is a coin flip in CI and never fails here

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0075 *(reopened)* |
| Where | `scripts/single-instance-check.sh:93-98`, invoked as `single-instance` from `Makefile:414` and run by CI's `Container image` job |
| Evidence | **Measured, and it corrects this row's own first version, which said timing rather than code.** Polling `pg_isready` continuously from container start against `postgres:17-alpine`: `................RRR.....RRRRRRRR…` — ready for three polls, **not-ready for five**, then ready permanently. One `R` to `.` transition, which is the temporary server going down. It reproduced on both runs of the same commit and in opposite directions: `32078341466` failed and `32079716931` passed on `5e0fb30`, then `32081422004` failed and `32081417936` passed on `fe4791e`. The naive double-check could not be reproduced as a failure on this machine over six attempts, and that is consistent rather than contradictory — the loop breaks after two attempts here, so the sleep cadence clears the gap |
| Severity | **Medium, and it is the gate rather than the product.** Nothing about the product is wrong and the check has never once failed for the reason it exists. But it is the gate LNK-M-0072's *a single container is still a supported configuration* rests on, it blocks the release PR, and a gate that answers differently twice for one tree teaches everyone to re-run it — which is how a gate stops being one. The fix is to require the ready state to **hold** rather than to appear once: consecutive successes inside the loop, with no separate confirming shot after it |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** |
| Closed by | **Owner-scheduled 2026-08-18**, outside any milestone — *the phase/PR cannot be considered complete unless all tests succeed appropriately* — so it lands as a task-class commit under the scope gate rather than by reopening a `done` row. **Fixed by asking over TCP instead of the container's unix socket**, which removes the race rather than widening the wait: the entrypoint runs the `initdb` temporary server with `listen_addresses=''`, so it has no TCP listener and cannot be seen. Measured both ways from container start — socket `........RR...RRRR`, TCP `............RRRRR`, **zero** ready-to-not-ready transitions on TCP. It is also the honest question, since the container under test reaches Postgres across a docker network and never over that socket. A three-success streak stays as belt and is documented as belt: a first attempt used a streak **alone** and was caught by measurement, because one run's temporary server answered ready for exactly three consecutive polls. There is no check after the loop; a single shot outside it was the defect. **Sabotage-verified against the new mechanism** — the real server started with `listen_addresses=''` makes the check refuse after its budget with *Postgres never became ready*, where the old code passed on the socket; restored by counter-edit, byte-identical |
| Status | closed |
| LinkCtrl | F256 |

## LNK-F-0257

**The container image is private, so the quick start in `README.md` does not work for anybody who is not signed in to GitHub — and it has been that way since 0.2.0**

finding · 2026-08-18

cites: [LNK-M-0072](milestones.md#lnk-m-0072)

**The container image is private, so the quick start in `README.md` does not work for anybody who is not signed in to GitHub — and it has been that way since 0.2.0.** README's quick start is `docker compose up -d --wait`, and `docker-compose.yml` resolves the image to `ghcr.io/devofpie/linkctrl:latest`. A stranger following the page gets an authorization failure, not a running instance. Nothing in the build is wrong: the workflow pushes `linux/amd64,linux/arm64` with `provenance: true` and `sbom: true` and all three tags. It is the package's **visibility** setting alone

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | — *(post-release verification, 0.3.0)* |
| Where | `README.md:55-72` (the quick start and *the latest tag is `0.3.0`*), `docker-compose.yml:19,23`, `docs/deployment.md:502` and `docs/releasing.md:125,174` — every published instruction naming the image — against the package's visibility, which is a setting rather than a file |
| Evidence | **Probed anonymously, the way an operator would, and the method validated against a known-public package.** `GET https://ghcr.io/token?scope=repository:devofpie/linkctrl:pull` returns **no token** for any tag — `0.3.0`, `0.3`, `latest` **and `0.2.0`**, so this predates this release; the same request for `homebrew/core/git` returns a token and the manifest answers **200**. Authenticated inspection then fails **403** as well, so the account running the check cannot confirm the manifest list, the provenance or the SBOM by pulling — the multi-arch build is evidenced from the workflow log and the digest `sha256:cc528255…` matches what the release body advertises |
| Severity | **High for a self-hostable product, and it is the first instruction a new reader follows.** No defect in the code, the image or the release notes; the failure is that the artifact those notes point at cannot be fetched. The fix is one setting and belongs to somebody with admin on the package — Package settings, *Change visibility*, Public — after which the manifest list, the platform pair, the provenance and the SBOM should be re-verified by pulling, which is the half this row could not do |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** |
| Closed by | **Closed 2026-08-18**, by the owner making the package public — a setting, so there is no diff for the fix itself and this cell is the record. **Re-verified anonymously, `docker logout` first, which is the half the row said it could not do.** The manifest is an OCI index at `sha256:cc528255…`, **matching the digest the release body advertises**, carrying real `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` manifests plus one attestation each — provenance is SLSA `buildDefinition`, SBOM is SPDX from syft, both per platform. `0.3.0`, `0.3` and `latest` all resolve to that one digest. Pulled and run, it reports `v0.3.0 (commit a19937417294, go1.26.6)` — the same commit as the binaries — and runs as `nonroot:nonroot`. **And the published image was put through the conformance gate itself**, `single-instance-check.sh ghcr.io/devofpie/linkctrl:0.3.0`: redirect, invalidation, dashboard, jobs, rate limiting and a boot against an unreachable Redis all pass, so the artifact a stranger pulls is one that satisfies LNK-M-0072's guarantee rather than one that merely built. **One correction the row itself needed**: it named the tags `v0.3.0` and `v0.2.0`, and no such tags exist — `docker/metadata-action`'s `{{version}}` strips the prefix. The finding was unaffected, since a private package refuses the token before any tag is looked at, but the cited strings were wrong and are fixed above |

## LNK-F-0262

**The CI `image` job now needs a Go toolchain it never installs**

finding · 2026-08-18

**The CI `image` job now needs a Go toolchain it never installs.** LNK-M-0079 made the WASM test fixtures a prerequisite of `single-instance`, and `single-instance` is a prerequisite of `ci-image-smoke` — the one CI job with a Docker daemon and, uniquely among the four, **no `actions/setup-go` step**. | Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0079 |
| Where | `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `image` job, whose only steps are buildx, two `build-push-action` calls and `make ci-image-smoke`; the other three jobs — `build`, `lint`, `integration` — each install Go deliberately, which `grep -n 'setup-go' .github/workflows/ci.yml` counts at three against four jobs. The chain was `single-instance`'s `addon-fixtures` prerequisite → the `$(ADDON_FIXTURE_DIR)/%.wasm` pattern rule, whose recipe is the `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build`; `grep -n 'wasip1 GOARCH' Makefile` is the recipe and `grep -n '^single-instance:' Makefile` the target whose prerequisite the resolution below replaced with a tolerated `$(MAKE) addon-fixtures` line. Cited by name rather than by line because every one of those numbers moved inside the milestone that wrote them (D224) |
| Evidence | Read from both files on 2026-08-18 while adding the add-on limb to the gate, and the cost was stated in the Makefile comment at the time rather than discovered later. **Not driven on a runner** — that is the whole of what is unverified here. GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` image does ship a Go toolchain, so the step is expected to work; `go.mod` says `go 1.26.5`, so a runner on an older minor downloads the toolchain under `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto`, which needs network the job already has |
| Severity | **Low, and it fails loudly rather than quietly** — a missing `go` makes `make ci-image-smoke` fail on a binary rather than on anything about the image, and F255's gate now asks whether CI is green. What it costs is that a gate this repository relies on rests on an unpinned property of somebody else's VM image, which is exactly the bar `golangci-lint`, the Tailwind CLI and three vendored assets are all pinned against. The fix is one `actions/setup-go` step in the `image` job — **which is `.github/workflows/` and therefore `ci/proposed/`'s route and the owner's to apply**, and that is why this is a row rather than an edit |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0079**, in the milestone that opened it, under phase-loop.md's in-spec exception — named in the commit message, as that rule requires. **The fix is not the `actions/setup-go` step this row proposed**, which was `ci/proposed/`'s route and the owner's to apply. Two changes remove the dependency instead: `single-instance` now *attempts* `addon-fixtures` and tolerates the failure, and `scripts/single-instance-check.sh` **skips its add-on limb** when there is no module rather than hard-failing, saying which prerequisite was missing. So the `image` job no longer needs a Go toolchain: it uses one when the runner image ships one and drives all three limbs, and drives two when it does not. `make addon-fixtures` still fails loudly on its own, and `make single-instance` on a developer machine still builds a module and runs the limb, so the gate m60.md asks for is unchanged. What is given up is stated: a runner that stopped shipping Go would drop limb three quietly rather than loudly. That was judged the smaller loss against a conformance gate whose prerequisite is an unpinned property of somebody else's VM image — the reasoning is D220, which also records why the proposal route was refused. |

## LNK-F-0263

**`addon.Host` has no synchronization, and two of its three methods are exported for milestones that will call them from request paths**

cites: [LNK-M-0088](milestones.md#lnk-m-0088)

**`addon.Host` has no synchronization, and two of its three methods are exported for milestones that will call them from request paths.** `Close` sets `runtime` and `loaded` to nil while `Addons()` and `Len()` read them, with nothing between the two. Unreachable today — the only caller is a `defer` in `main`, so the close happens after every reader has stopped — which is exactly the shape of a race that a later milestone introduces without touching the type

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0079 |
| Where | `internal/addon/host.go`'s `Host.Close` holds the two nil assignments — `grep -n 'h.runtime = nil' internal/addon/host.go` and the `h.loaded = nil` beside it — against the reads in `Host.Addons` and `Host.Len`, which is what `grep -n 'func (h \*Host)' internal/addon/host.go` enumerates in full: three methods, one of them the mutator. The sole caller is the `addons.Close(context.Background())` inside the `defer` that follows `addon.Open` in `cmd/linkctrl/main.go` — `grep -n 'addons.Close' cmd/linkctrl/main.go`. The milestones that will hold a reference on a serving path are **LNK-M-0083** (an add-on reaches the page) and **LNK-M-0086** (add-ons on the redirect path), and `Loaded.Module` — `grep -n 'func (l Loaded) Module' internal/addon/host.go` — exists for precisely that. **Cited by name throughout** (D224): every line number this row was written with pointed into the file LNK-M-0080 edits first, and one of them was already wrong when the row was written — `:146` was blank space below `LoadError`, not `Module()` |
| Evidence | Read from the type on 2026-08-18 during LNK-M-0079's review, and left out of spec deliberately: m60.md claims a lifecycle — discovered, verified, instantiated or refused — and says nothing about concurrent access, so a mutex here would be a claim the milestone does not make. **Not driven, and not drivable now**: `-race` cannot flag a race that has one goroutine, which is why this is a reading rather than a failing test |
| Severity | **Low today, high at LNK-M-0083.** The type is a boot-time singleton with a single-threaded lifecycle, so nothing can hit it. What makes it worth a row is that the fix belongs to whichever milestone first hands a `*Host` to a handler, and that milestone will be reading its own bullets rather than this type's history. An `RWMutex` around the three methods is the whole of it; the alternative is to make `Close` the only mutator and document the type as boot-only, which LNK-M-0088's runtime install/remove then contradicts |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** |

## LNK-F-0264

**`internal/addon`'s test helper reads the fixture it may be concurrently building, outside the lock that serializes the build**

finding · 2026-08-18

cites: [LNK-M-0079](milestones.md#lnk-m-0079)

cites: [LNK-M-0095](milestones.md#lnk-m-0095)

cites: [LNK-D-0415](decisions.md#lnk-d-0415)

cites: [LNK-D-0416](decisions.md#lnk-d-0416)

**`internal/addon`'s test helper reads the fixture it may be concurrently building, outside the lock that serializes the build.** `fixture()` reads the output path before `buildFixture` takes `builds.Mutex`, and reads it again after that function has returned and released it. So a caller can read the file while another goroutine's `go build -o` is truncating and rewriting the same path, and get a partial module — whose sha256 is not the sha256 of the bytes `addon.Open` then reads from disk, so the load is **refused** and the test fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the host

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0079 |
| Where | `internal/addon/host_test.go`: the two `os.ReadFile` calls in `fixture` — `grep -n 'os.ReadFile' internal/addon/host_test.go` — against the `builds.Lock()` at the top of `buildFixture` that neither is inside. Twelve callers, all in that file: `grep -c 'fixture(t' internal/addon/host_test.go` |
| Evidence | Read from the helper on 2026-08-18, during LNK-M-0079's fourth review. **Unreachable today, and therefore not driven**: `grep -rn 't.Parallel()' internal/addon/` returns nothing, and Go runs a package's tests one at a time unless a test asks otherwise, so two callers of `fixture()` are never in flight together. It goes live the first time a test in this package calls `t.Parallel()`, and `-race` will not flag it then either — the conflict is over a file, not over memory |
| Severity | **Low today, and it arrives as a flake.** The window is a cold fixture directory — a fresh clone, or a run after the built modules are removed — and only with a parallel caller present. What makes it worth a row is the failure it produces: a digest mismatch, which is exactly what LNK-M-0079's corrupt-a-byte test asserts on purpose, so the flake reads as the feature working rather than as a broken helper. The fix is to hold `builds.Mutex` across the read as well as the build, or to have `buildFixture` return the bytes it just wrote |
| Reviewed | **Reviewed 2026-09-04**, LNK-M-0095's triage — Tier B, approved for the close (D415, D416). The previous state is what the triage read. |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0095.** Both reads are inside `builds.Mutex`. The window was a cold fixture directory plus a parallel caller, and what it produced was a digest mismatch — which is precisely what the corrupt-a-byte test asserts on purpose, so the flake would have read as the feature working. |
| Status | closed |
| LinkCtrl | F264 |

## LNK-F-0265

**A symlinked add-on directory is silently not an add-on, and the operator sentence does not cover the case**

finding · 2026-08-18

cites: [LNK-M-0088](milestones.md#lnk-m-0088)

cites: [LNK-M-0079](milestones.md#lnk-m-0079)

cites: [LNK-D-0224](decisions.md#lnk-d-0224)

cites: [LNK-M-0095](milestones.md#lnk-m-0095)

cites: [LNK-D-0415](decisions.md#lnk-d-0415)

cites: [LNK-D-0416](decisions.md#lnk-d-0416)

**A symlinked add-on directory is silently not an add-on, and the operator sentence does not cover the case.** Discovery asks `DirEntry.IsDir()`, which is `lstat`-based, so `addons/current -> addons/oidc-1.2.0` — the ordinary versioned-install pattern, and the shape **LNK-M-0088**'s runtime install/remove will want, since an atomic swap of `current` is how a version is rolled forward — is logged as *"ignoring a non-directory in the add-ons directory"* and skipped. The instance then boots without that add-on, and a manifest saying `required` does **not** stop it: the entry is skipped before `ReadManifest` is reached, so the class that would have made this an outage instead of a silence is never read. It is also asymmetric with the root: `config.Validate` stats `LINKCTRL_ADDONS_DIR` itself with `os.Stat`, which **follows** symlinks, so the directory may be a symlink and the add-ons inside it may not. `docs/configuration.md` tells the operator only that *"a file that is not a directory is ignored with a warning, so a `README` you left in there is not an outage"* — **which does not read as covering a symlink *to* a directory**, and is the sentence to correct whichever way LNK-M-0088 answers

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0079 |
| Where | The discovery test and the warning beside it: `grep -n 'e.IsDir()' internal/addon/host.go` and `grep -n 'ignoring a non-directory' internal/addon/host.go`. The root's own check, which uses the following form: `grep -n 'os.Stat(c.Addons.Dir)' internal/config/config.go`. The operator sentence: `grep -n 'A file that is not a directory' docs/configuration.md`, under *What happens when an add-on will not load*. Cited by name (D224) |
| Evidence | **Driven on 2026-08-18**, during LNK-M-0079's sixth build, against a directory holding `oidc-1.2.0/` and `current -> oidc-1.2.0`: `os.ReadDir` reports `IsDir()=false Type()=L---------` for `current` and `IsDir()=true` for the real directory, while `os.Stat` on both says `IsDir()=true`. So the skip is the documented non-directory path taken against something that is a directory by every test but the one being used. Not driven **through `Open`** deliberately: a test asserting the current behaviour would be a claim m60.md does not make, and the mechanism is `os.ReadDir`'s, not this package's |
| Severity | **Low today, and it is a decision rather than a defect — LNK-M-0088's.** Nothing is broken for an operator who installs by copying a directory, which is what the documentation describes. What makes it worth a row is that resolving it is not one `os.Stat`: following a symlink means a module **outside** the operator-owned directory can be loaded, and `docs/configuration.md`'s trust boundary is drawn around exactly that directory — *"who may write to the directory is the whole of the boundary"*. So the fix is a choice about what an install *is*, which belongs to the milestone that builds installing (**LNK-M-0088**), together with the doc sentence and a boundary statement for whichever answer it takes |
| Reviewed | **Reviewed 2026-09-04**, LNK-M-0095's triage — Tier B, approved for the close (D415, D416). The previous state is what the triage read. |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0095, the documentation half.** `docs/configuration.md` states that a symlink is one of the ignored entries, that `current -> oidc-1.2.0` therefore loads nothing and a `required` class does not turn that into an outage, and that the directory itself may be a symlink while its contents may not. **The behaviour is carried and the question is named rather than answered**: following one means loading a module from outside the directory the trust boundary is drawn around. |
| Status | closed |
| LinkCtrl | F265 |
