## LNK-F-0266

**The two fixture builders disagree about when a WASM module is stale, so `make test` can run against a module `task test` would have rebuilt**

finding · 2026-08-18

cites: [LNK-F-0259](#lnk-f-0259)

cites: [LNK-M-0079](milestones.md#lnk-m-0079)

cites: [LNK-F-0264](#lnk-f-0264)

cites: [LNK-M-0080](milestones.md#lnk-m-0080)

cites: [LNK-F-0262](#lnk-f-0262)

**The two fixture builders disagree about when a WASM module is stale, so `make test` can run against a module `task test` would have rebuilt.** The Makefile's pattern rule makes each `.wasm` depend on its module's `main.go` **alone**, while its recipe compiles the whole package directory — so a fixture module that grows a second `.go` file is still built from that file and is no longer rebuilt when it changes. The Taskfile's `addon-fixtures` runs `go build` over every module unconditionally, so the mirror cannot go stale at all. Two builders, two staleness rules, one target name. **Same class as open F259** — the Taskfile mirror running something weaker than the Makefile under the same name — and two of them now argue the mirror needs one mechanism rather than two hand-maintained lists

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0079 |
| Where | Makefile: `grep -n 'ADDON_FIXTURE' Makefile` gives the `ADDON_FIXTURES` wildcard over `*/main.go`, the `$(ADDON_FIXTURE_DIR)/%.wasm: $(ADDON_FIXTURE_SRC)/%/main.go` pattern rule, and the recipe that builds `./$(ADDON_FIXTURE_SRC)/$*` — a directory, not the prerequisite. Taskfile: `grep -n 'addon-fixtures' Taskfile.yml` gives the task whose `cmds` loop rebuilds every module each run, and `grep -n 'sources:' Taskfile.yml` returns **nothing**, so no task in the mirror uses Task's own up-to-date mechanism. The reader that consumes whatever is on disk without asking is `fixture()` — `grep -n 'os.ReadFile(path)' internal/addon/host_test.go` |
| Evidence | Read from both files on 2026-08-18 while splitting the cost measurement, which is what made the pattern rule's single prerequisite visible. **Not driven, and not drivable today**: both fixture modules are one `main.go` each — `ls internal/addon/testdata/modules/*/` — so nothing exists for the divergence to bite on, which is also why it would arrive as a stale artifact rather than as an error. What is verified is the asymmetry itself: make rebuilt nothing when only a non-`main.go` input could have changed, because there is no such input for it to depend on |
| Severity | **Low, and it fails as a green run against old bytes.** The failure is a load that succeeds against yesterday's module, or a digest mismatch, in the one package whose whole subject is verifying that bytes are the bytes a manifest describes — so the flake reads as the feature working, exactly as F264 does. The fix is not symmetrical, which is why it is a row: a pattern rule cannot take a `$(wildcard)` over its own stem, so the Makefile side is either a per-module prerequisite list or an order-only dependency on the directory, while the Taskfile side is one `sources:`/`generates:` pair. Whether the mirror should carry two hand-maintained lists at all is F259's question, and the two want answering together |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** |
| Closed by | **Closed by LNK-M-0080**, under phase-loop.md's deferred-overlap rule rather than by owner approval: LNK-M-0080's own bullet says the LNK-M-0079 test modules *"are rebuilt on top of [the SDK], which is the first proof the SDK compiles a working consumer"*, and under a rule watching `main.go` alone a change to the **SDK** does not rebuild a fixture — so that proof could be a stale artifact. The exception is named in the commit message. Fixed in all three places rather than two, because the divergence stopped being theoretical the moment a shared input existed: the Makefile's pattern rule takes `.SECONDEXPANSION:` and a `$(wildcard)` over its own stem plus every `sdk/*.go`, which the row's own fix note said a pattern rule could not do; the Taskfile's task takes the first `sources:`/`generates:` pair in that file; and `fixture()` compares the same mtimes, because the release workflow and the CI image job reach it without a make target at all (F262). **Driven on the way in, not after**: the two-add-on scoping test failed against a `probe.wasm` built before an edit to its own source, which is exactly the stale artifact this row predicted, reported as a guest panic. **F259's question is not answered** — the mirror still carries hand-maintained lists, and now three of them rather than two. |
| Status | closed |
| LinkCtrl | F266 |

## LNK-F-0267

**A `degrade` add-on whose initialization never returns hangs the boot forever, and no milestone owns a load-time deadline**

finding · 2026-08-18

cites: [LNK-M-0079](milestones.md#lnk-m-0079)

cites: [LNK-D-0225](decisions.md#lnk-d-0225)

cites: [LNK-M-0086](milestones.md#lnk-m-0086)

cites: [LNK-D-0269](decisions.md#lnk-d-0269)

cites: [LNK-D-0272](decisions.md#lnk-d-0272)

cites: [LNK-D-0273](decisions.md#lnk-d-0273)

cites: [LNK-D-0274](decisions.md#lnk-d-0274)

cites: [LNK-F-0287](#lnk-f-0287)

cites: [LNK-M-0084](milestones.md#lnk-m-0084)

cites: [LNK-F-0274](#lnk-f-0274)

**A `degrade` add-on whose initialization never returns hangs the boot forever, and no milestone owns a load-time deadline.** Package initialization runs *while* a module is being instantiated — that is what makes a load-time failure expressible at all — so a module that spins there never reaches the code that reads its failure class. No listener comes up, no metric is written, and the class it declared is never consulted.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0079 |
| Where | `grep -n 'InstantiateModule' internal/addon/host.go` — the call takes the caller's context and nothing else; `grep -rn 'WithTimeout\|WithDeadline' internal/addon/ cmd/linkctrl/main.go` returns nothing, and the context handed in is the process's `signal.NotifyContext`. The claim it falsifies is this milestone's own: `grep -n 'degrade' docs/configuration.md` and `.env.example`, *"logs, counts and lets the instance serve without it"* — **both were corrected in LNK-M-0079's own commit to name this gap**, so what stays open is the deadline and not the sentence |
| Evidence | **The shape is already built and driven.** D225 records a busy-loop `init` added to the `minimal` fixture to force the instantiation timing red: it measured **15.00 s** in instantiation while compilation stayed at 390 ms, which is the same hang with a bound around it. Nothing recovers on its own — `grep -n 'CloseOnContextDone' internal/addon/host.go` is what makes SIGTERM still end the process, so an operator can kill it, having been told it would serve |
| Severity | **Medium, and it is availability rather than correctness.** An add-on nobody at this project wrote can stop an instance from starting whatever class it declares, which is the premise of the `degrade` class rather than a corner of it. Not in LNK-M-0079's spec — its bullet is satisfied by a module that *fails*, and both such modules are tested. Not LNK-M-0086's either: `grep -n deadline docs/build-notes/phase-details/m66.md` scopes that milestone's deadline to the **redirect path**, so a load-time bound is owned by nobody. Fix is a context with a timeout around instantiation and a class to put the expiry in; the choice of default is the part that needs an owner |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** Found by LNK-M-0079's sixth review, 2026-08-18. |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0079**, 2026-08-20, the reopening D269 scheduled (D272, D273, D274). **This row and F287 are one defect filed twice**, and this is the earlier filing — LNK-M-0079's own sixth review, 2026-08-18, against LNK-M-0084's re-finding two days later. The work that closed F287 closed this at the same moment: each add-on's load is given a budget of its own, the class the manifest declared decides what expiry costs, and a ninth outcome `load_timeout` puts the add-on's name in the log line and in the metric. ## LNK-F-0268

**`config_get` publishes a distinction the manifest format cannot carry: "declared with an empty default" and "declared no default" are the same value**

finding · 2026-08-19

cites: [LNK-M-0080](milestones.md#lnk-m-0080)

cites: [LNK-D-0224](decisions.md#lnk-d-0224)

cites: [LNK-M-0089](milestones.md#lnk-m-0089)

cites: [LNK-M-0095](milestones.md#lnk-m-0095)

cites: [LNK-D-0415](decisions.md#lnk-d-0415)

cites: [LNK-D-0416](decisions.md#lnk-d-0416)

**`config_get` publishes a distinction the manifest format cannot carry: "declared with an empty default" and "declared no default" are the same value.** The host answers `StatusNotFound` when a declared setting's default is the empty string, while the ABI's own definition of the function promises *"a declared setting with no value yet answers with the default the manifest gave it, and ErrNotFound only when it declared none"* — a sentence generated verbatim into the SDK an add-on reads and into the published table. `Setting.Default` is a `string` with `omitempty`, so `"default": ""` and an absent key decode to one value and no host could tell them apart. The **behaviour** is right for every setting that exists today; the **contract** claims a branch that cannot be reached

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0080 |
| Where | `grep -n 's.Default == ""' internal/addon/hostabi.go` is the branch; `grep -n 'ErrNotFound only when' internal/addon/abi/functions.go` is the promise, and `grep -rn 'ErrNotFound only when' sdk/ docs/addon-abi.md` is the same sentence on the three generated faces of it; `grep -n 'Default string' internal/addon/manifest.go` is the `omitempty` that collapses the two cases. Cited by name rather than by line (D224): every one of these files is generated or was written this milestone |
| Evidence | Read from the two files on 2026-08-19, during LNK-M-0080's second build, while making the record-level cookie change. **Not driven, and not drivable** — that is the finding: no test can distinguish two manifests that decode to the same `Manifest` value, so there is no red to show. What is verified is the collapse itself, which is `encoding/json` behaviour on a `string` field and not this package's |
| Severity | **Low, and it is a published sentence rather than a defect.** Nothing an add-on does today can observe the difference, because the only source of a value is a manifest default and `secret` may not carry one at all. What makes it worth a row is that the sentence crosses a repository boundary in an SDK doc comment, and the deprecation policy this milestone wrote makes *changing which status a function returns for a case it already handled* breaking — so the cheap fix stops being cheap once a release has shipped. **LNK-M-0089** is the milestone that supplies real setting values, and it is where the distinction acquires a meaning: a value the manager saved as empty is not the same as one never saved. Either the sentence is narrowed to what the format can carry, or the format grows a pointer or a `declared` flag and the sentence stays |
| Reviewed | **Reviewed 2026-09-04**, LNK-M-0095's triage — Tier B, approved for the close (D415, D416). The previous state is what the triage read. |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0095.** The sentence is narrowed to what the manifest format can carry — `ErrNotFound` means not declared, or declared with no default and no value, and the format cannot tell an empty default from an absent one, so the two are one case. Narrowing rather than growing the format: the deprecation policy makes changing a status for a case already handled a breaking change, so the cheap fix stops being cheap once a release ships. Regenerated into the SDK and the published table, which is where the sentence crosses a repository boundary. |
| Status | closed |
| LinkCtrl | F268 |

## LNK-F-0269

**The `//go:wasmimport` half of the SDK is analysed by nothing, and the comment beside it says the opposite**

finding · 2026-08-19

cites: [LNK-M-0080](milestones.md#lnk-m-0080)

cites: [LNK-D-0224](decisions.md#lnk-d-0224)

cites: [LNK-M-0095](milestones.md#lnk-m-0095)

cites: [LNK-D-0415](decisions.md#lnk-d-0415)

cites: [LNK-D-0416](decisions.md#lnk-d-0416)

cites: [LNK-D-0434](decisions.md#lnk-d-0434)

**The `//go:wasmimport` half of the SDK is analysed by nothing, and the comment beside it says the opposite.** `sdk/runtime_other.go` explains that the package builds for every platform *"so that this repository's linters and `go vet ./...` see the SDK at all"*. They see the **native twins**. Everything that only exists under `//go:build wasip1 && wasm` — every `//go:wasmimport` declaration, the whole `unsafe` surface, and the grow-and-retry loop in each of the six wrappers with an out parameter — is outside `make lint`, `make vet`, `go vet ./...` and CI's lint job alike, because none of them names a GOOS and the host's is not wasip1. So the only file in this repository whose subject is a foreign calling convention is the one file no analyser reads, and the sentence that would have told a reader so claims the reverse

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0080 |
| Where | The two files: `grep -n 'go:build wasip1' sdk/*.go` gives `abi_gen_wasip1.go` and `runtime_wasip1.go`. The overclaiming sentence is `grep -n 'see the SDK at all' sdk/runtime_other.go`. Nothing sets a GOOS: `grep -n GOOS .golangci.yml` is empty, `grep -n wasip1 Makefile` returns only the fixture build recipe at `:534`, and `grep -n golangci .github/workflows/ci.yml` names the pinned action while `grep -n GOOS .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns nothing. Cited by name rather than by line (D224): every file here is generated or was written this milestone |
| Evidence | **`go list` answers it directly**, on 2026-08-19: `go list -f '{{.GoFiles}} {{.IgnoredGoFiles}}' ./sdk` reports `GoFiles: [abi_gen.go abi_gen_other.go doc.go runtime_other.go]` and `Ignored: [abi_gen_wasip1.go runtime_wasip1.go]` — the toolchain states the exclusion itself, so no test is needed to show it. **There is no defect behind it**: `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go vet ./sdk/` is clean today, run the same day. That one line is also what makes this cheap to close, which is why it is in the evidence rather than left to be rediscovered |
| Severity | **Low today and structural, which is the combination that makes it a row rather than an edit.** Nothing is wrong now, and the wasip1 side is exercised end to end by three fixture modules and the outside-this-repository consumer test — a compile is a stronger check than vet in one respect and no check at all in the others. What the blind spot costs is the next change: `unsafe.Pointer` arithmetic, a `KeepAlive` the generator forgets to emit, or a loop bound that stops terminating would all reach `main` green. The fix is one line in the lint and vet targets, and the reason it is not a one-line edit here is that it belongs with a decision about **where**: a second `golangci-lint run` under a GOOS the linter must be told about, or a `go vet` step, or a build-tag matrix, and whichever is chosen has to run in CI as well as on this machine — the F255 shape exactly. **The sentence is deliberately left standing**: correcting it alone would remove the visible symptom and leave the gap, and this row is what keeps both together |
| Reviewed | **Reviewed 2026-09-04**, LNK-M-0095's triage — Tier B, approved for the close (D415, D416). The previous state is what the triage read. |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0095, D434.** `make vet` runs a second pass under `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm` over `./sdk/`. Demonstrated rather than argued: a scratch defect in `runtime_wasip1.go` is invisible to `go vet ./...` and caught by the new pass. **No CI proposal is needed and that was checked** — `vet` is already a prerequisite of `ci-build` and the workflow runs `make ci-build`. The declined shapes and the cost of this one (vet is a weaker net than golangci-lint) are on record in D434 and in the target's comment. |

**The SDK is the third generated artifact and only one of three gates knows it exists.** `make check-generate` regenerates it and diffs, so CI covers it. What makes it a row is that closing it properly touches three files and **two of them are not the loop's**: `workflow.md` is a process change that commits on its own, and `.github/workflows/` goes to `ci/proposed/`. | Reviewed | **Reviewed 2026-09-04**, LNK-M-0095's triage — Tier B, approved for the close (D415, D416). The previous state is what the triage read. |

## LNK-F-0274

**A migration that never returns hangs the boot *and* makes every other replica wait, and it is the one piece of an add-on's own code that nothing bounds**

finding · 2026-08-19

cites: [LNK-M-0079](milestones.md#lnk-m-0079)

cites: [LNK-D-0273](decisions.md#lnk-d-0273)

cites: [LNK-M-0082](milestones.md#lnk-m-0082)

cites: [LNK-D-0224](decisions.md#lnk-d-0224)

cites: [LNK-F-0267](#lnk-f-0267)

cites: [LNK-F-0306](#lnk-f-0306)

cites: [LNK-D-0275](decisions.md#lnk-d-0275)

**A migration that never returns hangs the boot *and* makes every other replica wait, and it is the one piece of an add-on's own code that nothing bounds.** An add-on's migrations are run by the host before the listener opens, with **no `statement_timeout`** — `AddonStatementTimeout` is set per transaction on the *query* path only, by `AddonDB.pin`, and `MigrateAddon` sets none — and they run while holding a Postgres session-level advisory lock. So `DO $$ BEGIN LOOP END LOOP; END $$`, or `SELECT pg_sleep(86400);`, in a `.sql` the manifest names and digests correctly hangs this replica forever, and every other replica then blocks in goose's lock retry for its five-minute ceiling before failing rather than starting. One bad add-on release therefore takes a whole rolling deploy down, where a module that hangs takes one replica down at a time. **This is the direction LNK-M-0079's load budget is deliberately pointed away from**: D273 bounds compiling and instantiating the *module* and leaves the storage step on the parent context, because LNK-M-0082 gives migrations five minutes to wait for this same lock and a budget over the whole load would make that wait unreachable. The bound for this one belongs on the migration connection, which is Postgres's to enforce

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0082 |
| Where | `grep -n 'AddonStatementTimeout' internal/store/addons.go` — set in `AddonDB.pin` and nowhere in `MigrateAddon`; `grep -n 'WithLockTimeout' internal/store/addons.go` for the five-minute retry the other replicas spend. The window is `grep -n 'openStorage' internal/addon/host.go`, called from `loadOne` before the module is instantiated and on the parent context by design — `DefaultLoadTimeout`'s comment says why. Cited by name (D224) |
| Evidence | **Not driven, and the reason is that driving it means hanging a test.** What is verified is the absence: `pin` is the only site that sets a statement timeout and it is reached from `Query` and `Exec` only, so no timeout is in force while `provider.Up` runs. The lock's ceiling is read from `lock.WithLockTimeout(5, 60)` in `MigrateAddon`, which is goose's period-and-threshold form — 60 attempts at 5 seconds. The fix is a `statement_timeout` on the migration connection, which is one runtime parameter and is cheap, and the number is the decision: **the other fix this cell used to name — the load-time deadline applied to migrations as well as to instantiation — was overruled by D273 at LNK-M-0079's reopening and is recorded here rather than deleted, because a position that leaves a tracker without a line saying it was overruled is indistinguishable from a row somebody edited by accident.** too tight and a legitimate `CREATE INDEX` on a large table fails an upgrade, which is the case LNK-M-0082 chose five minutes for. m63.md's own risks name the migration that **fails** and not the one that never finishes |

## LNK-F-0276

**`AddonMaxResultBytes` does not bound the host's heap, and its comment said it did**

finding · 2026-08-19

cites: [LNK-M-0082](milestones.md#lnk-m-0082)

cites: [LNK-D-0224](decisions.md#lnk-d-0224)

**`AddonMaxResultBytes` does not bound the host's heap, and its comment said it did.** The check in `encodeRows` runs *after* `rows.Values()` and `json.Marshal(row)` have materialized one row, and after pgconn has read the whole `DataRow` off the wire — so a single row larger than the megabyte is allocated in full before the refusal, times `AddonMaxConns` concurrent callers. An add-on may store an arbitrarily large value in its own schema, deliberately: there is no quota there, which is m63.md's own answer. So `SELECT huge_column FROM mine` allocates the value four times over and the bound refuses it afterwards. The **returned result** is bounded, which is what the ABI promises an add-on; the host's memory is not.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0082 |
| Where | `grep -n 'buf.Len()+len(encoded)' internal/store/addons.go` is the check, and the two lines above it are `rows.Values()` and `json.Marshal` — the order is the whole finding. The comment corrected in this milestone is `grep -n 'not a bound on the host' internal/store/addons.go`. Cited by name (D224) |
| Evidence | **Read from the tree rather than driven, and the reason is that driving it means allocating a gigabyte in a test.** What is verified is the order: the bound is compared against `buf.Len()+len(encoded)`, so `encoded` exists before the comparison, and `encoded` is `json.Marshal` of a `map[string]any` built from `rows.Values()`. Nothing between the wire and that map consults any bound; `maxStringIn` (64 KiB) bounds what a *guest* hands the host and not what Postgres hands the host |
| Severity | **Low, and it is a memory bound rather than a boundary.** No confinement claim rests on it: the add-on is spending its own schema's disk to allocate the host's memory, which it can also do by holding its four connections, and `AddonStatementTimeout` bounds how long. What makes it a row is that the fix is not obvious — bounding it properly means refusing a row by width before decoding, which pgx exposes only through the raw `pgconn` result reader, so it is a rewrite of `encodeRows` rather than a moved `if`. The comment is corrected in this milestone; the bound is this row |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** Found by LNK-M-0082's review, 2026-08-19, and filed at the review's instruction. |
| Status | open |
| LinkCtrl | F276 |

## LNK-F-0277

**`EnsureAddonSchema` is not serialized across replicas, unlike the migrations it precedes**

finding · 2026-08-19

cites: [LNK-M-0082](milestones.md#lnk-m-0082)

cites: [LNK-D-0224](decisions.md#lnk-d-0224)

cites: [LNK-M-0079](milestones.md#lnk-m-0079)

**`EnsureAddonSchema` is not serialized across replicas, unlike the migrations it precedes.** The goose session lock is taken inside `MigrateAddon`; the schema creation, the role creation and the `ALTER ROLE … PASSWORD` run *before* it and outside it, and the existence-check-then-`CREATE ROLE` is not atomic even inside its own transaction. Two replicas cold-starting together race: the loser's transaction rolls back whole and its add-on load answers `OutcomeStorageFailed`, and a `required` add-on then stops that replica. The credential is a second race in the same window — replica B's `ALTER ROLE` can land between replica A's `EnsureAddonSchema` and A's `MigrateAddon`, which fails A's migration connection outright, since the re-mint added in this milestone covers `AddonDB`'s pool and not the migration connection. Both recover on restart, which is why it is a row rather than a repair.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0082 |
| Where | `grep -n 'func EnsureAddonSchema' -A 30 internal/store/addons.go` for the unlocked transaction, `grep -n 'NewPostgresSessionLocker' internal/store/addons.go` for where the lock starts, and `grep -n 'EnsureAddonSchema\|MigrateAddon' internal/addon/host.go` for the order at the call site — the lock begins one function later. Cited by name (D224) |
| Evidence | **Read from the tree, not driven**: driving it means two processes cold-starting into one database inside `go test`, which the integration harness has no shape for. What is verified is the ordering — `EnsureAddonSchema` takes no advisory lock and no `pg_advisory` call appears anywhere in it — and that the failure is loud: `openStorage` returns the error, `loadOne` records `OutcomeStorageFailed`, and LNK-M-0079's class rule stops the boot for a `required` add-on |
| Severity | **Low, and it is a cold-start race with a loud failure and a restart-shaped recovery.** The fix is to take the add-on's own migration lock **around** `EnsureAddonSchema` as well, which is a few lines and one ordering decision — the lock currently belongs to goose, taken inside the provider, so the host would have to take one of its own first. It is a row rather than an edit because m63.md's bullet asks for *the same goose session-lock serialization across replicas* for the **migrations**, which the tree has, and widening that to the role and schema creation is a design choice about who owns the lock |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** Found by LNK-M-0082's review, 2026-08-19, and filed at the review's instruction. |
| Status | open |
| LinkCtrl | F277 |

## LNK-F-0278

**The connection budget guard does not see add-on pools, and both operator documents tell you to plan against a total the add-ons are not in**

finding · 2026-09-04

cites: [LNK-M-0082](milestones.md#lnk-m-0082)

cites: [LNK-D-0224](decisions.md#lnk-d-0224)

cites: [LNK-M-0095](milestones.md#lnk-m-0095)

cites: [LNK-D-0415](decisions.md#lnk-d-0415)

cites: [LNK-D-0416](decisions.md#lnk-d-0416)

**The connection budget guard does not see add-on pools, and both operator documents tell you to plan against a total the add-ons are not in.** `internal/config` refuses `DB_MAX_CONNS + DB_REDIRECT_MAX_CONNS > 90` and says the reason is the shipped `max_connections` of **100**; `docs/configuration.md` and `docs/deployment.md` each tell an operator to keep that sum under the server's limit. Each storage add-on now holds up to `AddonMaxConns` (**4**) permanently plus **one** migration connection at boot, and none of that is in the sum or in either document — `docs/addon-abi.md` states the figure to the add-on *author*, who is not the person tuning the pools. So an instance tuned at the guard's ceiling of 90 exceeds 100 with three storage add-ons and the guard reports nothing; the defaults, 20 and 6, leave room for several, which is why this is a row rather than a repair.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0082 |
| Where | The guard is `grep -n 'DB_REDIRECT_MAX_CONNS' internal/config/config.go` — the comparison and its `max_connections of 100` message. The add-on's cost is `grep -n 'AddonMaxConns' internal/store/addons.go` and the `stdlib.OpenDB` in `MigrateAddon` beside it. The two documents are `grep -n 'max_connections' docs/configuration.md docs/deployment.md`; the third, which does not reach an operator, is `grep -n 'four connections' docs/addon-abi.md`. Cited by name (D224) |
| Evidence | **Arithmetic against the shipped compose file, read rather than driven**: `grep -n 'max_connections' docker-compose.yml` is 100, the guard's ceiling is 90, `AddonMaxConns` is 4, and nothing in `internal/config` mentions add-ons at all — `grep -in 'addon' internal/config/config.go` is empty. Driving it means booting an instance with three storage add-ons at `DB_MAX_CONNS=84`, which the harness has no shape for and which the arithmetic settles |
| Severity | **Low at the defaults and moderate for an operator who tuned to the ceiling.** The failure is *FATAL: sorry, too many clients already* at a boot or at an add-on's first busy moment, not corruption. The fix is not only a widened comparison: the guard runs before any add-on is discovered, so it would have to count installed modules that declared `storage.own_schema` — which is a config-validation pass that reads the add-on directory, an ordering change rather than an arithmetic one — or the documents grow the term and the operator does the arithmetic. Choosing between those is what makes it a row |
| Reviewed | **Reviewed 2026-09-04**, LNK-M-0095's triage — Tier B, approved for the close (D415, D416). The previous state is what the triage read. |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0095, the documentation half.** `docs/configuration.md` and `docs/deployment.md` both state the add-on term — four connections per storage add-on while loaded, one more at boot, outside the guard's sum because the guard runs before any add-on is discovered — and give the operator the arithmetic. **The guard itself is carried**: counting installed modules means config validation reading the add-ons directory, which is an ordering change rather than a widened comparison. |

## LNK-F-0279

**A `WITH HOLD` cursor holds a temporary file for the life of a pooled connection, and it is an object in no catalogue, so the confinement's shape cannot see it**

finding · 2026-08-19

cites: [LNK-D-0251](decisions.md#lnk-d-0251)

cites: [LNK-M-0082](milestones.md#lnk-m-0082)

cites: [LNK-D-0224](decisions.md#lnk-d-0224)

cites: [LNK-F-0276](#lnk-f-0276)

**A `WITH HOLD` cursor holds a temporary file for the life of a pooled connection, and it is an object in no catalogue, so the confinement's shape cannot see it.** `AddonConfinementViolations` asks `pg_shdepend` and `pg_depend` — both catalogues of *objects* — and a temporary **file** is neither. Through the write path, `DECLARE big CURSOR WITH HOLD FOR SELECT g, repeat('x',900) FROM generate_series(...)` is accepted, the per-call `COMMIT` materializes it, and the file stays in `base/pgsql_tmp` until the backend ends — which for a pgxpool means across ABI calls, times `AddonMaxConns`. It needs no privilege, and `restrictDatabaseTemp` does not reach it because temp *files* are not temp tables. So the post-condition is empty and both gauges read 0 while the disk fills. The bound that exists, `ALTER ROLE addon_<name> SET temp_file_limit`, needs **superuser** — which is D251's shape exactly, a narrowing rather than a boundary — and once a superuser has set it the role can neither raise nor reset it, and the cursor then dies with *temporary file size exceeds temp_file_limit*.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0082 |
| Where | The catalogues the check consults are `grep -n 'pg_shdepend' -A 20 internal/store/addons.go` in `AddonConfinementViolations`; the revoke that does not reach it is `grep -n 'func restrictDatabaseTemp' internal/store/addons.go`. The per-call commit that materializes the cursor is `grep -n 'func (a \*AddonDB) Exec' -A 20 internal/store/addons.go`. The sentences corrected in this milestone rather than left false are `grep -n catalogu` and `grep -n stored` over `internal/store/addons.go docs/SECURITY.md Plan.md CHANGELOG.md internal/observability/metrics.go` — two greps rather than one alternation, because this table's rows are cells and a regex alternation character splits one. This row first cited `catalogued` alone, which is the spelling in two of the five files and misses the *stored* half entirely, metrics.go carrying only that one. Cited by name (D224) |
| Evidence | **Driven, over the mapped port, as a role built statement for statement the way `EnsureAddonSchema` builds one and with `AddonDB.Exec`'s transaction, pins and timeout reproduced.** A 600,000-row `WITH HOLD` cursor put **553,197,568 bytes** into one `pgsql_tmp` file, `pg_ls_tmpdir()` reported the same size on two samples ten seconds apart while the session slept, and the count went to **0** the moment the connection closed. `pg_stat_database.temp_bytes` did **not** move while the file existed — it is charged when the file is removed — so a `temp_bytes` alert is not a substitute either. The privilege half was driven both ways: `ALTER ROLE … SET temp_file_limit` answers *permission denied to set parameter* as a NOSUPERUSER CREATEROLE role **and** as the add-on's own role, succeeds as superuser, and with 64 MB in force the same cursor fails at the `COMMIT` with *temporary file size exceeds temp_file_limit (65536kB)*. LNK-M-0082's third review measured the same shape at 2.82 GB for a 3,000,000-row cursor. Every role created for the measurement was dropped |
| Severity | **Low, and it is a resource residual rather than a confinement failure.** Nothing is read, nothing is written outside the schema, and nothing survives the connection — an add-on can already spend the host's memory (F276) and hold its four connections for as long as `AddonStatementTimeout` allows. What makes it a row is that the only available bound needs a privilege this product does not ask operators for, so closing it means either adding *superuser at install time* to `docs/deployment.md` — which would undo the reason `CREATEROLE` was chosen — or asking for `temp_file_limit` as an optional hardening step the host verifies and reports rather than sets. That is a documentation-and-defaults decision, not a code change, which is why it is filed instead of fixed |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** Found by LNK-M-0082's third review, 2026-08-19, and filed at its instruction; re-measured independently by the fourth worker before filing. |
| Status | open |
| LinkCtrl | F279 |

## LNK-F-0280

**The confined role can rewrite its own password, so the credential is not only the host's and outlives the process**

finding · 2026-08-19

cites: [LNK-D-0249](decisions.md#lnk-d-0249)

cites: [LNK-M-0082](milestones.md#lnk-m-0082)

cites: [LNK-D-0224](decisions.md#lnk-d-0224)

**The confined role can rewrite its own password, so the credential is not only the host's and outlives the process.** `EnsureAddonSchema` mints a fresh password at every load and stores it nowhere, which is the design — but Postgres lets any role change its own password and offers no way to withhold that from one. `ALTER ROLE CURRENT_USER PASSWORD 'x'` is accepted through the ordinary write path, and a session then authenticates as the add-on's role with `x`; it persists in `pg_authid` across shutdown until the next load's `ALTER ROLE … PASSWORD` replaces it. **What such a session is worth is more than that add-on's schema**: it also carries `EXECUTE` on the advisory-lock functions, which Postgres grants to `PUBLIC` and this product cannot revoke, and the product's lock keys are compile-time constants in a public repository (D249). `releaseLocks` bounds a hold to one statement **for connections through the host's own pool** and governs nothing about a session opened from outside it. So a published module can set a password its author knows and hold one of the product's job locks from anywhere that can reach Postgres.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0082 |
| Where | The mint is `grep -n 'func EnsureAddonSchema' -A 40 internal/store/addons.go`, at the `ALTER ROLE … LOGIN PASSWORD`; the sentence corrected in this milestone rather than left false is `grep -n 'claim about the host' internal/store/addons.go` and `grep -n 'worth is more than' docs/SECURITY.md`. The lock release that does not reach an outside session is `grep -n 'func.*releaseLocks' -A 15 internal/store/addons.go`. Cited by name (D224) |
| Evidence | **Driven over the mapped port as a role built statement for statement the way `EnsureAddonSchema` builds one, with a wrong password refused first so the login is real SCRAM.** `ALTER ROLE CURRENT_USER PASSWORD 'authorknows'` -> `ALTER ROLE`, and `psql` then authenticated as the role with that password. `ALTER ROLE CURRENT_USER PASSWORD NULL` -> `ALTER ROLE`, after which every connection answers 28P01 and `rolpassword IS NULL` reads **t** to the application. The four attributes an earlier round measured as refused are still refused to the role: `NOLOGIN` and `CONNECTION LIMIT 0` answer *permission denied to alter role*, and `SELECT rolpassword FROM pg_authid` answers *permission denied for table pg_authid* — refused on the read path, reachable on the write path. `pg_try_advisory_lock(4242)` and `has_function_privilege(role,'pg_advisory_lock(bigint)','EXECUTE')` both answer **t** as that role. Every role created for the measurement was dropped |
| Severity | **Low as deployed, and it is not fixable in Postgres.** A role can always change its own password; there is no per-role deny and no event trigger for `ALTER ROLE`. Exposure needs network reach to Postgres with password authentication, which the documented deployment does not give — the database is on the compose network and the port is bound to loopback. The availability limb self-heals: a nulled password gives 28P01 and `AddonDB.acquire`/`reauthenticate` re-mint. What could be done is detection rather than prevention — comparing `pg_authid.rolpassword` against the hash of the credential the host issued, at the same load-time point the confinement post-condition runs — which is a design choice about whether the host keeps a hash it currently keeps nothing of, and that is why this is a row |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** Found by LNK-M-0082's fifth review, 2026-08-19, and filed at its instruction; re-measured independently by the sixth worker before filing. |
| Status | open |
| LinkCtrl | F280 |

## LNK-F-0281

**An add-on that is installed but did not load is reported as an orphan, and every operator-facing sentence calls an orphan uninstalled**

finding · 2026-08-30

cites: [LNK-M-0089](milestones.md#lnk-m-0089)

cites: [LNK-M-0082](milestones.md#lnk-m-0082)

cites: [LNK-D-0224](decisions.md#lnk-d-0224)

cites: [LNK-M-0094](milestones.md#lnk-m-0094)

cites: [LNK-M-0095](milestones.md#lnk-m-0095)

cites: [LNK-D-0415](decisions.md#lnk-d-0415)

cites: [LNK-D-0416](decisions.md#lnk-d-0416)

cites: [LNK-D-0428](decisions.md#lnk-d-0428)

**An add-on that is installed but did not load is reported as an orphan, and every operator-facing sentence calls an orphan uninstalled.** `Host.OrphanSchemas` subtracts `h.Schemas()`, which is built from `h.loaded`. A `degrade`-class add-on whose module fails to instantiate never enters `h.loaded`, and neither does one whose manifest fails validation while its schema survives from an earlier good version — so its schema is warned about at boot as having no loaded module while the add-on is still installed on disk. m63.md's bullet is **literally satisfied**: it says *no matching loaded module*. What is out of step is everything a person reads — Plan.md, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/SECURITY.md` and the boot warning each frame an orphan as an add-on that was **uninstalled**. It bites at the consumer m63.md names: LNK-M-0089's *orphaned data named explicitly* row would offer a still-installed add-on's data for purge.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0082 |
| Where | `grep -n 'func (h \*Host) OrphanSchemas' -A 20 internal/addon/host.go` and the append that feeds it, `grep -n 'h.loaded = append' -B 15 internal/addon/host.go` — the `continue` fifteen lines above it is the `degrade` path that leaves a schema and appends nothing. The boot warning is `grep -n 'no loaded module' internal/addon/host.go`; the sentences that say *uninstalled* are `grep -n 'removing an add-on does not remove' Plan.md` and `grep -in 'Removing an add-on' CHANGELOG.md docs/SECURITY.md docs/operations.md`. Cited by name (D224) |
| Evidence | **Read from the tree rather than driven**, because driving it means a module that instantiates once and then fails to instantiate on a later boot with its schema intact — two hosts over one database with a swapped artifact, which the harness has no shape for. What is verified is the set difference: `OrphanSchemas` is `AddonSchemas` minus `h.Schemas()`, `h.Schemas()` reads `h.loaded`, and `loadOne` appends to `h.loaded` only after the module instantiates — so every failure path between `EnsureAddonSchema` and that append produces a schema no loaded module claims |
| Severity | **Low, and it is naming rather than behaviour.** Nothing is deleted in this milestone, so the cost today is one misleading boot warning. It becomes a real cost in **LNK-M-0089**, which offers orphaned data for purge from a page: an operator told that a still-installed add-on's schema is orphaned may purge data the add-on is about to need at its next successful load. The fix belongs there and is a distinction the enumeration cannot currently make — *installed but not loaded* against *not installed at all* — which means LNK-M-0089 reads the add-on directory rather than `h.loaded`, or the host records what it discovered separately from what it loaded. **Raised to High at LNK-M-0094, 2026-08-30: the prediction came true and LNK-M-0089 shipped without the fix.** Driven end to end against a real database — a `degrade`-class add-on with storage, one good load, then an `abi_version` bump — printing `manager list has 0 rows`, `ORPHAN ROW: name=abibump`, `PURGE SUCCEEDED for a still-installed add-on` and `SCHEMA DROPPED`. So it is no longer naming: it is unrecoverable deletion of a still-installed add-on's rows, reached by an operator following a confirmation dialog that asserts the false premise — `internal/ui/templates/pages/addons.html:105` and `:241` are two further instances of the wrong sentence, now beside a destructive control, with the add-on absent from the list above so nothing contradicts them. Two narrowings the drive established: a `required`-class failure is fatal so no purge surface exists, and at least one prior successful load is needed. Loss is bounded — role, identity links and settings survive `manager.go:373-386`, and migrations re-run at the next successful load, so the add-on returns structurally intact with empty tables |
| Reviewed | **Reviewed 2026-09-04**, LNK-M-0095's triage — Tier A, approved for the close (D415, D416). The previous state is what the triage read. |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0095.** `addonSet` gains `discovered` — every add-on installed on disk, recorded in `Open`'s loop above every refusal branch and maintained by `Install` and `Remove` — and `OrphanSchemas` subtracts that rather than `h.loaded`, which is D428's *at the source* answer over the two cheaper ones. The boot warning now reads *belonging to no installed add-on*. Driven by `TestAnInstalledAddonThatDidNotLoadIsNotAnOrphan`: one good load, then a `degrade`-class `abi_version` bump, and the schema is not offered for purge. Sabotage-verified — removing the subtraction reddens it naming this row. |
| Status | closed |
| LinkCtrl | F281 |

## LNK-F-0282

**`LINKCTRL_MIGRATE_ON_START=false` does not reach an add-on's DDL, so the change-controlled deployment shape and the storage capability are only partly compatible**

finding · 2026-08-19

cites: [LNK-M-0082](milestones.md#lnk-m-0082)

cites: [LNK-M-0088](milestones.md#lnk-m-0088)

**`LINKCTRL_MIGRATE_ON_START=false` does not reach an add-on's DDL, so the change-controlled deployment shape and the storage capability are only partly compatible.** The host applies a storage add-on's migrations at every boot, before the listener, whatever the flag says, and no `lctl` command applies them out of band.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0082 |
| Where | `grep -rn MigrateOnStart --include=*.go` finds it in exactly three places — the config field, the `store.Migrate` call and the partition call — and none of them is `MigrateAddon`, which `grep -n MigrateAddon internal/addon/host.go` reaches from `openStorage`. `grep -n 'migrate up' cmd/lctl` runs `store.Migrate` only |
| Evidence | **Four shipped operator claims are false in the presence of a storage add-on**, and none was written by this milestone: `grep -n MIGRATE_ON_START docs/cli.md docs/configuration.md docs/deployment.md docs/releasing.md` — each promises migrations become a deliberate step. **All four were corrected in LNK-M-0082's own commit to say the flag governs the product's schema only**, so what stays open is the behaviour, not the documentation |
| Severity | **Low as a defect and a real question as scheduling.** No data is at risk and the ordering is the one m63.md asks for. What makes it a row rather than an edit is that **gating it has a cost the loop may not choose**: under `false` a `required` storage add-on could not load at all, so change-controlled deploys and add-on storage become mutually exclusive unless `lctl` grows a command that applies an add-on's migrations. That is a new command, a new failure surface and an owner's call — probably **LNK-M-0088**'s, since runtime install and remove is where an out-of-band apply belongs |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** Found by LNK-M-0082's sixth review, 2026-08-19. |
| Status | open |
| LinkCtrl | F282 |

**`template_render` is declared, is backed by LNK-M-0083, and LNK-M-0083 implemented rendering without it — so the ABI's published table describes a function this milestone was supposed to bring to life and did not.** Its doc says it *"renders one of this add-on's own templates through the host's renderer"*, which means a module ships template **source**; LNK-M-0083 answered the rendering half by having a module return **text** the host wraps and escapes (D259), because the milestone's own risk requires an add-on's output to be *"always data, never template"* and markup a module wrote is not data. The function is therefore still `Live: false` while `BackedBy: "M64"`, and the `routes.own_prefix` permission doc still promises "render its own templates through the host's renderer" — a half-promise on a surface another repository compiles against

What makes it a row rather than an edit is that all three are changes to a published contract, and the worker that would have made one is the same actor that chose D259 |

## LNK-F-0284

**Cross-site unsafe methods to an add-on's routes are 403, and it is not conditional on credentials — so an OIDC `response_mode=form_post` callback is refused while a server-to-server webhook passes**

finding · 2026-08-21

cites: [LNK-M-0083](milestones.md#lnk-m-0083)

cites: [LNK-M-0085](milestones.md#lnk-m-0085)

cites: [LNK-M-0092](milestones.md#lnk-m-0092)

cites: [LNK-M-0088](milestones.md#lnk-m-0088)

cites: [LNK-M-0089](milestones.md#lnk-m-0089)

cites: [LNK-D-0291](decisions.md#lnk-d-0291)

cites: [LNK-M-0081](milestones.md#lnk-m-0081)

**Cross-site unsafe methods to an add-on's routes are 403, and it is not conditional on credentials — so an OIDC `response_mode=form_post` callback is refused while a server-to-server webhook passes.** `http.CrossOriginProtection` refuses *every* cross-site unsafe request, not only a cookie-authenticated one, and LNK-M-0083 mounted add-on routes inside the application chain that carries it. A form-post callback is a browser navigation from the identity provider's origin, so it arrives cross-site and never reaches the module; a webhook from a server sends no `Sec-Fetch-Site` and reaches it. **`same-site` is refused too**, so a provider on a sibling subdomain of the dashboard is refused as well. Not false for any LNK-M-0083 bullet — the routes work, the middleware is right, and the milestone is not the one that builds a callback — which is why it is a row. **Addressed to LNK-M-0085**, which builds an authentication flow on exactly this path and therefore has to answer it: the choices are a trusted-origin registration an add-on's manifest declares, an exemption bounded to a declared callback path, a `code`-flow-only stance that never posts, or nothing, deliberately. **LNK-M-0092's acceptance test is where an unanswered version of this surfaces** — the OIDC add-on is the first real consumer, so a 403 discovered there arrives in the milestone least able to absorb it, after LNK-M-0085, LNK-M-0088 and LNK-M-0089 have all been built on the assumption that a callback lands

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0083 |
| Where | `internal/httpx/router.go` — the add-on patterns are registered on `appMux`, whose chain in `NewRouter` applies `http.NewCrossOriginProtection().Handler(appHandler)` to everything on it; the comment beside the registration was corrected in LNK-M-0083's own diff, where it had claimed the middleware applies *"to a cookie-authenticated unsafe method"*. `internal/addon/http.go` is unreached |
| Evidence | Measured through `NewRouter` with a real module behind the route, POST to `/addons/probe/callback`: `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` **403**, `same-site` **403**, `same-origin` **200**, `none` **200**, header absent **200**. The module was not entered in either 403 |
| Severity | **Medium, and it is scheduling rather than a defect.** The behaviour is the correct default and the cost is that the surface LNK-M-0083 exists to enable has one shape it cannot serve. Whichever way LNK-M-0085 answers it, the answer is a change to what a cross-origin request may do to this product, so it is the owner's |
| Reviewed | **Unreviewed.** |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0085**, 2026-08-21, by D291 — **the stance, and no exemption.** The row's four options were: a trusted-origin registration the manifest declares, an exemption bounded to a declared callback path, a `code`-flow-only stance, or nothing deliberately. The owner took the third. Nothing is exempted from the cross-site refusal, so there is no carve-out to get wrong — the argument that decided it was that this phase had just spent four workers watching carve-outs leak in LNK-M-0081 — and the two declined options are recorded in the entry rather than left as *we decided this did not matter*. **The cost is published in the two places the row's disposition implies and the decision required**: `docs/addon-abi.md` has a section addressed to the publisher (*Your callback arrives as a redirect*), naming the measured statuses and saying that a provider offering only `form_post` cannot be used, and `docs/configuration.md`'s *When an add-on signs people in* says the same thing to the operator. The behaviour is unchanged — nothing in the middleware moved and no test of it was touched — which is what makes this a closure by decision rather than by work. **What LNK-M-0085 added on top of the row's own scope** is the consequence of a GET callback nobody had written down: the cross-site refusal does not reach a GET, so an add-on's callback carries its own CSRF exposure and the `state` parameter is the add-on's to get right. The ABI page says so at `identity_link` and in the same section, because the host's guarantee — a link is only ever made for whoever is signed in, in their own browser, now — is narrower than a publisher would assume from the rest of the boundary. LNK-M-0092's provider is still to be checked against `form_post` **before** LNK-M-0092, which is the row's own instruction and is not this milestone's to discharge. |
| Status | closed |
| LinkCtrl | F284 |

## LNK-F-0285

**The log sanitizer passes 260 variation selectors, so a module that declared nothing carries a covert channel into the operator's log**

finding · 2026-08-20

cites: [LNK-D-0242](decisions.md#lnk-d-0242)

cites: [LNK-M-0084](milestones.md#lnk-m-0084)

cites: [LNK-D-0240](decisions.md#lnk-d-0240)

cites: [LNK-M-0081](milestones.md#lnk-m-0081)

cites: [LNK-D-0270](decisions.md#lnk-d-0270)

cites: [LNK-D-0269](decisions.md#lnk-d-0269)

cites: [LNK-D-0283](decisions.md#lnk-d-0283)

cites: [LNK-D-0284](decisions.md#lnk-d-0284)

cites: [LNK-D-0285](decisions.md#lnk-d-0285)

cites: [LNK-F-0310](#lnk-f-0310)

cites: [LNK-D-0286](decisions.md#lnk-d-0286)

**The log sanitizer passes 260 variation selectors, so a module that declared nothing carries a covert channel into the operator's log.** `escapedRune` asks `unicode.Other_Default_Ignorable_Code_Point`, which is Unicode's *residue* property — the real set is `Default_Ignorable_Code_Point = Other_DI` union `Cf` union `Variation_Selector`, less `White_Space`, `FFF9..FFFB`, `13430..13440` and the prepended concatenation marks. Variation selectors are category `Mn`, so `unicode.IsGraphic` says yes and the default-deny fallback never reaches them. **The same failure shape as the hand-written list D242 replaced, one abstraction level up**: a property whose name begins with `Other_` is incomplete by construction.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0084 |
| Where | `internal/addon/hostabi.go:470-495` — the property test at `:491`, the fallback at `:494`. Falsifies `phase-details/m62.md:34-40`, `docs/SECURITY.md:81` and `docs/addon-abi.md:298-309`, each of which promises the graphic-yet-invisible set is escaped |
| Evidence | **Reproduced end to end twice, in two contexts that could not see each other**, through a module with `Permissions: nil`, under both the text and JSON handlers: a line reading *everything is fine* from which `SECRET=hunter2` was recovered, and a second line with no visible message at all. Go's tables were checked against Unicode's rather than assumed — `Other_DI` has 3776 members of which 7 are graphic, `Variation_Selector` has 260, all graphic, and **none of them is in `Other_DI`**; `Cf` intersected with graphic is empty, so the fallback covers `Cf` and cannot reach the selectors. Works with a U+E0100 byte-per-selector scheme and a U+FE00–FE0F nibble scheme, so it does not depend on plane-14 support. No downstream filter exists: `hostabi.go:109` is the only call site, `internal/observability/logging.go:19-35`'s `ReplaceAttr` touches attribute keys and never `msg`, `strconv.Quote` preserves anything `IsPrint`, and `Mn` is printable. `maxLogMessage` bounds one line at roughly 682–1024 payload bytes and nothing bounds the call rate |
| Severity | **High.** It is the one boundary D240 exists for, it is reachable by every loaded module including one that declared nothing, and three shipped documents state the opposite. Reliability of the *hiding* is renderer-dependent — browser log UIs render a selector after a non-emoji base as nothing, a bare terminal with a `.notdef`-drawing font may show narrow boxes — which narrows the concealment and not the defect |
| Reviewed | Yes — owner approved 2026-08-20 on LNK-M-0084's triage; **reopens LNK-M-0081**. The remedy is **D270** and was answered in the same breath, because escaping all 260 would make `hostabi_test.go:638`'s assertion about `❤️` false and that is a choice rather than a patch |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0081**, reopened 2026-08-20 under D269, closed by **D283** — which supersedes D270's remedy rather than implementing it. The derivation is kept and is the half of D270 nothing disputed: `defaultIgnorable` computes `Other_DI ∪ Cf ∪ Variation_Selector − White_Space − FFF9..FFFB − 13430..13440 − PCM`, all seven terms, and `TestNoDefaultIgnorableCharacterReachesALogLine` counts 4174 members and 267 graphic against the residue property's 3776 and 7 and asserts that no member of the derived set reaches a line as itself. The derivation as first written for this row had six of the property's seven terms and so claimed 4190, and the count sat inside a floor where a wrong constant reads the same as a Unicode revision; the seventh term and equalities for every stated number are **D284**. **The carve-out is gone: every variation selector is deleted from the message rather than escaped, with no base set and no exemption** (`strippedRune`). `❤️` becomes `❤`, still a heart; `😀` is untouched. Two narrower remedies were built and rejected before this one, and neither shipped — both are on the unmerged branch `wip/m62-sanitizer`, and D276 and D277 are their numbers, spent there and withdrawn. Attempt 1 keyed the exemption on category `So` and a progress bar drawn from `U+2588` and `U+2591` carried the secret through byte-identical at log₂3 bits per symbol; attempt 2 keyed it on Unicode's registered emoji variation sequences and was defeated in turn by building the channel from registered bases whose selector a renderer ignores. Stripping became available once the threat was read as **legibility rather than confidentiality** — `log` is ungated, so a module may write a secret in plain text regardless, and what the boundary owes is only that what a reader sees is what is there. The lossiness that buys is proved harmless in `TestStrippingIsLossyAndForgesNothing`: the boundary is the escaping form composed after a deletion, so its image is a subset of the escaping form's and a module reaches strictly fewer log lines than before; the record boundary, the `addon` and `source` attributes, and the truncation mark's doubled backslash are each unaffected. The three reproduction schemes and the block-element bar are kept as tests, driven both at the boundary function and end to end through the `undeclared` fixture. Three documents that promised the wrong thing are corrected — and `docs/SECURITY.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` are corrected twice over, because the shipped sentence *cannot arrange bytes in an operator's log to be overlooked* and the parked attempt's replacement *cannot put invisible bytes in an operator's log* are both false, and what stands now claims only what default-ignorability supports. **The claim was narrowed once more before this row landed (D285), and the remainder is F310.** *Invisible* is not a Unicode property and this row's fix does not enforce one: eight combining marks Unicode annotates as not visibly rendered are outside `Default_Ignorable_Code_Point` and reach a line as themselves. What bounds them is a property the tree now asserts rather than one that merely held — an add-on may post to the log and may not read it, driven over every function in the ABI by `TestAnAddonPostsToTheLogAndCannotReadItBack`. And the neutralization was reaching one host function while three documents claimed it for the module: manifest validation embeds a refused value with `%q`, which escapes neither `Mn` nor `Lo`, so a hostile name, version or migration filename reached an operator's log and an instance's fatal message untouched. **The site list was the wrong shape and was wrong twice — the second one missed `store.MigrateAddon`'s success-path line, in a package that cannot import the neutralizer, and the per-request instantiation failure — so the escaping is applied by the logger the subsystem writes through and by a single neutralizing exit on `Route`, and there is no list (D286).** |
| Status | closed |
| LinkCtrl | F285 |

## LNK-F-0286

**Duplicate and case-variant JSON keys defeat both the `schema_version` equality check and the permission declaration, so a manifest deceives every reader but the host**

finding · 2026-08-20

cites: [LNK-M-0084](milestones.md#lnk-m-0084)

cites: [LNK-M-0079](milestones.md#lnk-m-0079)

cites: [LNK-D-0269](decisions.md#lnk-d-0269)

cites: [LNK-D-0271](decisions.md#lnk-d-0271)

cites: [LNK-M-0092](milestones.md#lnk-m-0092)

**Duplicate and case-variant JSON keys defeat both the `schema_version` equality check and the permission declaration, so a manifest deceives every reader but the host.** `encoding/json` takes the **last** occurrence of a repeated key and matches struct tags case-insensitively when no exact match exists, so `SCHEMA_VERSION` and `Permissions` bind the same fields the documented lowercase spellings do. A manifest whose readable text says `"schema_version": 7` and `"permissions": []` loads as schema 1 holding four grants.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0084 |
| Where | `internal/addon/manifest.go:257-274` — `parseManifest`, with `DisallowUnknownFields` at `:259` and the trailing-document check at `:267`, and no duplicate-key check anywhere. The equality check it walks past is `:287-293`. Falsifies `phase-details/m60.md:32` and `phase-details/m62.md:41-43` |
| Evidence | **Reproduced through the real `Open` over a real installed directory, twice independently.** Loaded as `name=sneaky schema_version=1 grants=[config.read routes.own_prefix session.mint storage.own_schema]`. Battery: permissions listed then emptied is accepted with no grants; emptied then listed is accepted holding all three; `schema_version` 99 then 1 is accepted while 1 then 99 is refused; every field spelled in uppercase is accepted. **Nothing covers the manifest bytes** — the `sha256` field is the digest of the *module* (`internal/addon/host.go:668-671`) and `MigrationFile.SHA256` covers migration files (`internal/addon/migrations.go:89-92`); there is no canonicalization and no signature over `addon.json`. `ReadManifest` has exactly two call sites and everything downstream consumes the parsed struct, so the info gauge and the boot log report the truth. `manifest_test.go:86-88` covers a permission repeated *inside* the array and `:181` covers unknown fields; nothing covers a repeated key |
| Severity | **Medium-high.** Not a sandbox escape — an operator reading the boot log is not fooled. The deceived party is whoever reads the **file**, which is the artifact another repository is compiled against and the thing a reviewer inspects before installing. Both of the manifest's strictest rules are bypassable by a publisher |
| Reviewed | Yes — owner approved 2026-08-20 on LNK-M-0084's triage; **reopens LNK-M-0079**. Fix is self-contained: re-decode into `map[string]json.RawMessage` or walk the decoder's token stream in `parseManifest`, refusing exact repeats and case-collisions |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0079**, 2026-08-20, the reopening D269 scheduled (D271). `parseManifest` now walks the document's token stream against the Go type it decodes into and refuses two things: a key not spelled exactly as `docs/configuration.md` documents it, and a key that appears more than once. **Taken further than the row's fix note**, which said *exact repeats and case-collisions*: a lone `"Permissions"` with no lowercase twin is refused too, because the reasoning behind `DisallowUnknownFields` — a key this host does not know was written for a schema it does not implement — applies to spelling, and a second accepted spelling of every field is a second way to write the format `LinkCtrl-OIDC` compiles against. **Recursive**, so a `migrations` entry carrying `file` twice is refused as well; only the top level was reproduced, but that one names one `.sql` to a reader and hashes another. The key set is read from the struct tags rather than listed, so a field added later is covered without anybody remembering. The row's other observation — that nothing hashes `addon.json` — stands and is why exactness is the answer rather than tolerance; signing the manifest is LNK-M-0092's provenance question. Cost: the file is read into memory to be walked twice, so the read is bounded at 64 KiB — `maxManifestBytes`, which is its own constant and not the ABI's `maxStringIn`: the two are the same number for unrelated contracts, and aliasing them would have let a change made for an ABI reason move what manifests this host accepts. Documented in `docs/configuration.md`'s manifest section, because meeting an undocumented bound as a boot failure is the same experience as a bug. Sabotage, all restored by counter-edit: bypassing the check parses **10** cases, dropping the duplicate rule fails exactly the four repeat cases, dropping the recursion fails exactly the two nested ones, dropping the bound fails its own test |
| Status | closed |
| LinkCtrl | F286 |

## LNK-F-0287

**Nothing bounds load-time instantiation, so a `degrade`-class add-on hangs boot forever instead of being skipped**

finding · 2026-08-20

cites: [LNK-M-0084](milestones.md#lnk-m-0084)

cites: [LNK-M-0079](milestones.md#lnk-m-0079)

cites: [LNK-D-0269](decisions.md#lnk-d-0269)

cites: [LNK-D-0272](decisions.md#lnk-d-0272)

cites: [LNK-F-0305](#lnk-f-0305)

cites: [LNK-D-0273](decisions.md#lnk-d-0273)

cites: [LNK-M-0082](milestones.md#lnk-m-0082)

cites: [LNK-F-0274](#lnk-f-0274)

cites: [LNK-D-0274](decisions.md#lnk-d-0274)

cites: [LNK-F-0267](#lnk-f-0267)

**Nothing bounds load-time instantiation, so a `degrade`-class add-on hangs boot forever instead of being skipped.** The host instantiates with the context `Open` was given, and that context carries no deadline — so a module spinning in `init()` stops the instance ever listening, with no log line naming it, no metric and no error. The same gap gives an unbounded load-time log flood, since `log` is ungated, only one line's size is bounded, and `Open` will not return to stop it.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0084 |
| Where | `internal/addon/host.go:719-723` instantiates with `Open`'s context; `cmd/linkctrl/main.go:172` is `signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), …)` with no deadline, passed at `:280` **before the listener**. Falsifies `phase-details/m60.md:44-46` — *logs, increments a metric, and the instance serves without it* |
| Evidence | **Reproduced twice.** A `degrade`-class fixture spinning in `init()`: `Open` did not return within 20 s, and the only log line emitted was the guest's own. Compilation does not catch it — the spin is at instantiation — and there is no timeout in `loadOne` or its caller. **The runtime is already configured correctly**: `WithCloseOnContextDone(true)` is set, and with a 3 s deadline on `Open`'s context the second reproduction returned in 3.0023 s and logged `m60.md:44-46`'s contract verbatim, *add-on failed to load; the instance continues without it … failure_class=degrade error="module closed with context deadline exceeded"*. So the defect is one missing deadline and not a missing mechanism. Log flood measured at **3697 lines / 14.7 MiB in 2 s**. SIGTERM does cancel the hang, so *forever* is *until an operator kills it*; a boot that needs SIGTERM is still a hang |
| Severity | **Medium-high.** Falsifies a milestone bullet that is asserted by test for every other failure mode, and the failure is silent — nothing says which add-on boot is stuck on |
| Reviewed | Yes — owner approved 2026-08-20 on LNK-M-0084's triage; **reopens LNK-M-0079**. The fix is one `context.WithTimeout` around the call handed to `addon.Open`, and it has already been shown to produce the exact documented behaviour |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0079**, 2026-08-20, the reopening D269 scheduled (D272). `Open` gives each add-on's load a context of its own with a **30 s** deadline, and a ninth outcome `load_timeout` distinguishes *never returned* from *trapped*. **Per add-on rather than for the whole load**, which the row's fix note did not decide: a shared budget once expired is expired for every add-on behind the slow one, so one `degrade` module's hang would refuse a healthy `required` one and stop the instance — the very bullet this reopening repairs. Asserted, not argued: with a shared budget the test fails as `add-on "zfine": load_timeout`. 30 s is the number `TestInstantiationCostIsMeasured` has called the boundary since LNK-M-0079 shipped, and that test now reads the constant so the two cannot drift; one 1.87 MB fixture loads in 388 ms, measured 2026-08-20. The hazard the fix introduces is asserted too — `WithCloseOnContextDone` would close a healthy module if its load context outlived the load — by calling into a loaded add-on after its budget passed. **Sabotage: removing the deadline does not fail the test, it hangs it**, `panic: test timed out after 25s`, which is F287 reproduced through the shipped suite. **The log flood this row also names is bounded and not fixed** — 30 s of an ungated `log` is still roughly 200 MiB — and is F305, because log volume is no claim of `m60.md`'s. **Scoped at the second attempt** (D273): the budget is given to `CompileModule` and `InstantiateModule` and to nothing else, because laying it over the whole of `loadOne` also caps the five-minute migration-lock wait LNK-M-0082 chose to prevent a crash loop — this row's fix re-breaking a shipped milestone from the other side. What the budget therefore does not bound is F274. **Corrected again at the third attempt** (D274): the compile half was wrapped in `runGuest` and enforced by nothing. wazero checks the context while compiling only on its multi-worker path, and the single-worker branch it takes by default walks the code section with no check in it — so a compile past the budget returned a nil error, expiry is read only when a step errors, and the load simply finished late while four documents said it was bounded. `compileWorkers` is now on the context `CompileModule` runs under, and `TestTheCompileStepIsBounded` is red without it. **F267 is this row filed two days earlier** and is closed by the same work |
| Status | closed |
| LinkCtrl | F287 |

cites: [LNK-D-0281](decisions.md#lnk-d-0281)

**The per-database variant of a role GUC survives the load's reset, so a confined add-on parks memory settings that outlive every reboot.** `EnsureAddonSchema` issues `ALTER ROLE … RESET ALL`, which clears only the role's cluster-wide defaults in `pg_roles.rolconfig` (`setdatabase = 0`). `ALTER ROLE CURRENT_USER IN DATABASE <db> SET work_mem = '4GB'` writes to `pg_db_role_setting` with `setdatabase = <db oid>`, which that statement never touches. **The string `IN DATABASE` appears nowhere in `internal/`, `test/`, `decisions.md` or `docs/SECURITY.md`.**

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0084 |
| Where | `internal/store/addons.go:293` is the incomplete reset; `:266-267`'s comment — *Everything the role has been told about itself, cleared* — and D253's heading — *clears every role-level setting* — are both false. The confinement claim it bears on is `phase-details/m63.md:26` |
| Evidence | **Reproduced twice on Postgres 17.10 in `linkctrl-test-postgres-1`, through a statement-for-statement copy of `EnsureAddonSchema` → `OpenAddonDB` → `pin` → `Exec`.** After the host's `RESET ALL` and `search_path` re-set, the surviving row reads `linkctrl -> {work_mem=4GB, maintenance_work_mem=8GB}` and a fresh login reads `work_mem=4194304 src=database user`. Effect is live rather than nominal: a confined `READ ONLY` sort of 400,000 rows ran fully in memory (`Sort Method: quicksort Memory: 12289kB`) where the 4 MB default spills to disk. Every attack on it failed — a non-superuser alters its own per-database settings with no grant, since these are USERSET; there is no `SET ROLE` escape hatch because `addons.go:417-418` logs the pool in **as** the role, which is why startup applies the rows; `pin` (`addons.go:1195-1197`) pins only `search_path` and `statement_timeout`, and replaying inside that transaction still reads 4GB. **Wider than first filed**: `IN DATABASE <any name>` is accepted including databases the role cannot connect to, so a one-database repair is also incomplete, and no `DROP ROLE` path exists anywhere in the product, so the rows outlive uninstall. **The test that guards this is structurally blind** — `test/integration/addon_storage_test.go:1432` sets the plain variant and its verifier `roleConfig` at `:1484` reads only `pg_roles` |
| Severity | **Medium.** Not a data-boundary breach — it reads no other tenant's rows. It is a permanent, un-clearable resource-amplification foothold that the milestone claimed to have closed and asserts by a test that cannot see it. `work_mem=4GB` times `AddonMaxConns` per add-on, surviving every reboot, is a standing OOM lever against the shared cluster |
| Reviewed | Yes — owner approved 2026-08-20 on LNK-M-0084's triage; **reopens LNK-M-0082**. The fix is a second reset scoped `IN DATABASE current_database()`, and the test has to read `pg_db_role_setting` or it will pass over the fix as it passed over the defect |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0082**, reopened 2026-08-20 under D269, closed by D279 as amended by **D282**. The reset is now driven by `pg_db_role_setting` rather than by a scope: the load enumerates every database the role holds a row in, resets each, resets the cluster-wide row and then pins — because the second reset this row proposed, scoped `IN DATABASE current_database()`, is evaded by naming any other database, `IN DATABASE` taking a name rather than a connection and being accepted against `template0`. The structurally blind test is replaced rather than extended — three scopes set, `pg_db_role_setting` read — and `AddonConfinementViolations` gained the branch that reports a row surviving a load, in any database, which is what catches the repair failing later. **The uninstall half is answered by detection rather than by repair (D282, reversing D281).** A boot-time sweep over roles no add-on claims was built and removed: it identified its targets from the catalogue, and the `pg_auth_members` fact it rested on is written *automatically* for a `NOSUPERUSER CREATEROLE` creator — the privilege `docs/deployment.md` asks for — so it did not distinguish a role this product made from one an operator typed. What holds instead is the post-condition, which refuses an add-on whose role carries a parked row and therefore needs no proof of ownership at all. The residue is stated in `m63.md`, `Plan.md`, `docs/deployment.md` and `docs/operations.md` rather than swept: an uninstalled add-on's settings stay on a role nothing drops, inert because only a **login** reads one and nothing logs in as that role, cleared by the add-on's next load or by an operator's `ALTER ROLE … RESET ALL`. All false written claims are corrected: `addons.go`'s comment and `docs/SECURITY.md` in place, D253's heading by D279 and D281's identification clause by D282, because decisions.md is append-only. |

## LNK-F-0289

**An add-on holding only `routes.own_prefix` signs the visitor out, by volume rather than by naming**

finding · 2026-08-20

cites: [LNK-M-0084](milestones.md#lnk-m-0084)

cites: [LNK-M-0085](milestones.md#lnk-m-0085)

cites: [LNK-M-0083](milestones.md#lnk-m-0083)

cites: [LNK-D-0269](decisions.md#lnk-d-0269)

cites: [LNK-D-0287](decisions.md#lnk-d-0287)

**An add-on holding only `routes.own_prefix` signs the visitor out, by volume rather than by naming.** `decodeResponse` bounds neither the number of `Set-Cookie` entries a module returns nor a cookie value's length, and the handler writes every entry. 180 cookies inside the add-on's **own** declared prefix overflow the browser's per-domain cap and the session cookie is what the eviction takes.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Found in | LNK-M-0084 |
| Where | `internal/addon/http.go:504-509` loops `r.SetCookie` calling `checkCookie` per entry with no count bound; `internal/httpx/addons.go:199-214` writes them all. Falsifies `phase-details/m64.md:52` — *it cannot read the cookie, mint, or **destroy sessions** — that boundary is LNK-M-0085's subject and stays closed here* |
| Evidence | **Reproduced twice in real Chromium against a real signed-in account**, with headers byte-identical to the real handler's: n=179 leaves the visitor on `/dashboard` with the session cookie present; n=180 drops the store from 180 to 150 and lands on `/login?next=/dashboard` with the cookie gone. `linkctrl_theme`, a genuine host-set cookie, is evicted too. **Every mitigation was tried and failed.** `Secure` and `__Host-` give no protection, because the host applies `Secure` to the add-on's cookies from the same config (`internal/httpx/addons.go:207`), so the browser's non-secure-first purge cannot separate them — `__Host-linkctrl_session` was evicted at both n=179 and n=180. Recency gives none either: the flood request carries the session cookie and it is still the one taken. Driving the real handler with 1200 cookies writes **1200 headers, 107,000 bytes**, status 200; the only ceiling is the ABI's 64 KiB single-value bound on the response record, so it is incidental rather than a decision. `Max-Age=31536000` makes the occupation persistent. **One limb refuted**: the 60,124-byte `Set-Cookie` the host also emits is stored by no browser, Chromium capping name+value at 4096 — measured kept at 4000 and dropped at 4090 — so it is header bloat that cannot contribute to the eviction |
| Severity | **High, and narrower than *destroy sessions* reads.** Server-side sessions are untouched — five of five still live and unrevoked after the flood — the token stays valid and the add-on never learns it. What is achieved is a forced **client-side** sign-out of whoever visits the add-on's page, repeatable on every visit, from the cheapest possible grant with no session needed to trigger it. On LNK-M-0085's authentication add-on the same primitive is a sign-in loop. `internal/addon/manifest.go:434` is **not** falsified: it says no add-on may read or set the host namespace, and eviction is neither |
| Reviewed | Yes — owner approved 2026-08-20 on LNK-M-0084's triage; **reopens LNK-M-0083** |
| Closed by | **LNK-M-0083**, 2026-08-21, the reopening D269 scheduled (D287). The host writes no cookie a module named. It packs an add-on's cookies into one cookie of its own per lifetime class — `linkctrl_addon_<name>` and `…_kept`, inside the namespace no manifest may declare a prefix in — and `Route` **empties the module's list as it packs**, so the writer in `internal/httpx` has no path to that list at all. **Not the fix the row's severity cell implies**, and the reason is in D287: every threshold shape is wrong here, because a browser cookie is persistent and the add-on also decides how many responses there are, so a cap per response is that cap times however many visits it can arrange. What replaces it is occupancy fixed by the code: two slots, whatever a module answers and however often it is visited. **Measured in Chromium, where the finding was made**: with the flooding module installed on the test instance, 200 visits each setting a name never used before leave the store holding exactly `linkctrl_session` and one jar, the dashboard still answers signed in, and the module still reads back what it just wrote. In Go, against the real fixture and a model of a browser's store, the same 200 visits with the same result — and the writer test hands the real handler 1200 cookies a module named and asserts that **nothing** is written, which is the property rather than the bound. One threshold remains and is named as one: a jar holds 3 KiB, over which an add-on loses its own oldest values and the log names it. The two refuted limbs are not re-fixed — the 60 KB single cookie no browser stores, and `manifest.go`'s namespace message, which was never falsified. Sabotage, all restored by counter-edit: writing one cookie per entry fails four tests, dropping the jar-size refusal fails two, one jar for both lifetimes fails the lifetime test, dropping the log fails the full-jar test, and a writer that reaches for the module's list fails the writer test |
| Status | closed |
| LinkCtrl | F289 |
